href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1126788409"><div class="plainlist"><ul><li><a href="/wiki/.ua" title=".ua">.ua</a></li><li><a href="/wiki/.%D1%83%D0%BA%D1%80" <p><b>Ukraine</b> (<span class="rt-commentedText nowrap"><span class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt" lang="en-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<span style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><span title="/juː/: &#39;u&#39; in &#39;cute&#39;">juː</span><span title="/ˈ/: primary stress follows">ˈ</span><span title="&#39;k&#39; in &#39;kind&#39;">k</span><span title="&#39;r&#39; in &#39;rye&#39;">r</span><span title="/eɪ/: &#39;a&#39; in &#39;face&#39;">eɪ</span><span title="&#39;n&#39; in &#39;nigh&#39;">n</span></span>/</a></span>&#32;<span data-nosnippet="" id="ooui-php-1" class="ext-phonos ext-phonos-PhonosButton noexcerpt ext-phonos-PhonosButton-emptylabel oo-ui-widget oo-ui-widget-enabled oo-ui-buttonElement oo-ui-buttonElement-frameless oo-ui-iconElement oo-ui-buttonWidget" data-ooui="{&quot;_&quot;:&quot;mw.Phonos.PhonosButton&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;\/\/upload.wikimedia.org\/wikipedia\/commons\/transcoded\/a\/a8\/En-us-Ukraine.ogg\/En-us-Ukraine.ogg.mp3&quot;,&quot;rel&quot;:[&quot;nofollow&quot;],&quot;framed&quot;:false,&quot;icon&quot;:&quot;volumeUp&quot;,&quot;data&quot;:{&quot;ipa&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;text&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;lang&quot;:&quot;en&quot;,&quot;wikibase&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;file&quot;:&quot;En-us-Ukraine.ogg&quot;},&quot;classes&quot;:[&quot;ext-phonos&quot;,&quot;ext-phonos-PhonosButton&quot;,&quot;noexcerpt&quot;,&quot;ext-phonos-PhonosButton-emptylabel&quot;]}"><a class="oo-ui-buttonElement-button"><span class="oo-ui-iconElement-icon oo-ui-icon-volumeUp"></span><span class="oo-ui-labelElement-label"></span><span class="oo-ui-indicatorElement-indicator href="/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key" title="Help:Pronunciation respelling key"><i title="English pronunciation respelling">yoo-<span style="font-size:90%">KRAYN</span></i></a>; Ukrainian: <span lang="uk">Україна</span>, <small>romanized:&#160;</small><span title="Ukrainian-language romanization"><i lang="uk-Latn">Ukraina</i></span>, <small>pronounced&#160;</small><span title="Representation in the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA)" class="IPA" lang="uk-Latn-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/Ukrainian" title="Help:IPA/Ukrainian">[ʊkrɐˈjinɐ]</a></span>&#32;<span data-nosnippet="" id="ooui-php-2" class="ext-phonos ext-phonos-PhonosButton noexcerpt ext-phonos-PhonosButton-emptylabel oo-ui-widget oo-ui-widget-enabled oo-ui-buttonElement oo-ui-buttonElement-frameless oo-ui-iconElement oo-ui-buttonWidget" data-ooui="{&quot;_&quot;:&quot;mw.Phonos.PhonosButton&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;\/\/upload.wikimedia.org\/wikipedia\/commons\/transcoded\/b\/be\/Uk-%D0%A3%D0%BA%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%97%D0%BD%D0%B0_%282%29.oga\/Uk-%D0%A3%D0%BA%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%97%D0%BD%D0%B0_%282%29.oga.mp3&quot;,&quot;rel&quot;:[&quot;nofollow&quot;],&quot;framed&quot;:false,&quot;icon&quot;:&quot;volumeUp&quot;,&quot;data&quot;:{&quot;ipa&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;text&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;lang&quot;:&quot;en&quot;,&quot;wikibase&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;file&quot;:&quot;Uk-\u0423\u043a\u0440\u0430\u0457\u043d\u0430 (2).oga&quot;},&quot;classes&quot;:[&quot;ext-phonos&quot;,&quot;ext-phonos-PhonosButton&quot;,&quot;noexcerpt&quot;,&quot;ext-phonos-PhonosButton-emptylabel&quot;]}"><a role="button" tabindex="0" href="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/b/be/Uk-%D0%A3%D0%BA%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%97%D0%BD%D0%B0_%282%29.oga/Uk-%D0%A3%D0%BA%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%97%D0%BD%D0%B0_%282%29.oga.mp3" rel="nofollow" aria-label="Play audio" class="oo-ui-buttonElement-button"><span class="oo-ui-iconElement-icon oo-ui-icon-volumeUp"></span><span class="oo-ui-labelElement-label"></span><span class="oo-ui-indicatorElement-indicator oo-ui-indicatorElement-noIndicator"></span></a></span><sup class="ext-phonos-attribution noexcerpt"><a href="/wiki/File:Uk-%D0%A3%D0%BA%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%97%D0%BD%D0%B0_(2).oga" title="File:Uk-Україна (2).oga">i</a></sup>) is a country in <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Europe" title="Eastern Europe">Eastern Europe</a>. It is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_European_countries_by_area" title="List of European countries by area">second-largest European country</a> after <a href="/wiki/Russia" title="Russia">Russia</a>, which <a href="/wiki/Russia%E2%80%93Ukraine_border" title="Russia–Ukraine border">borders</a> it to the east and northeast.<sup id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-11">&#91;a&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-12">&#91;11&#93;</a></sup>  It also borders <a href="/wiki/Belarus" title="Belarus">Belarus</a> to the north; <a href="/wiki/Poland" title="Poland">Poland</a>, <a href="/wiki/Slovakia" title="Slovakia">Slovakia</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Hungary" title="Hungary">Hungary</a> to the west; and <a href="/wiki/Romania" title="Romania">Romania</a> and <a href="/wiki/Moldova" title="Moldova">Moldova</a><sup id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-13">&#91;b&#93;</a></sup> to the southwest; with a coastline along the <a href="/wiki/Black_Sea" title="Black Sea">Black Sea</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Sea_of_Azov" title="Sea of Azov">Sea of Azov</a> to the south and southeast.<sup id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-14">&#91;c&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Kyiv" title="Kyiv">Kyiv</a> is the nation's capital and <a href="/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Ukraine" title="List of cities in Ukraine">largest city</a>, followed by <a href="/wiki/Kharkiv" title="Kharkiv">Kharkiv</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dnipro" title="Dnipro">Dnipro</a> and <a href="/wiki/Odesa" title="Odesa">Odesa</a>. Ukraine's <a href="/wiki/Official_language" title="Official language">official language</a> is <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_language" title="Ukrainian language">Ukrainian</a>; <a href="/wiki/Russian_language_in_Ukraine" title="Russian language in Ukraine">Russian</a> is also widely spoken, especially in the <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Ukraine" title="Eastern Ukraine">east</a> and <a href="/wiki/Southern_Ukraine" title="Southern Ukraine">south</a>.
</p><p>During the <a href="/wiki/Middle_Ages" title="Middle Ages">Middle Ages</a>, Ukraine was the site of <a href="/wiki/Early_Slavs" title="Early Slavs">early Slavic</a> expansion and the area later became a key centre of <a href="/wiki/East_Slavs" title="East Slavs">East Slavic</a> culture under the state of <a href="/wiki/Kievan_Rus%27" title="Kievan Rus&#39;">Kievan Rus'</a>, which emerged in the 9th century. The state eventually disintegrated into rival regional powers and was ultimately destroyed by the <a href="/wiki/Mongol_invasion_of_Kievan_Rus%27" title="Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus&#39;">Mongol invasions</a> of the 13th century. The area was then contested, divided, and ruled by a variety of external powers for the next 600 years, including the <a href="/wiki/Polish%E2%80%93Lithuanian_Commonwealth" title="Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth">Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Austrian_Empire" title="Austrian Empire">Austrian Empire</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman Empire</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Tsardom_of_Russia" title="Tsardom of Russia">Tsardom of Russia</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Cossack_Hetmanate" title="Cossack Hetmanate">Cossack Hetmanate</a> emerged in <a href="/wiki/Central_Ukraine" title="Central Ukraine">central Ukraine</a> in the 17th century marked on maps as "Ukraine, land of the Cossacks", but was partitioned between Russia and Poland, and ultimately absorbed by the <a href="/wiki/Russian_Empire" title="Russian Empire">Russian Empire</a>. <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_nationalism" title="Ukrainian nationalism">Ukrainian nationalism</a> developed, and following the <a href="/wiki/Russian_Revolution" title="Russian Revolution">Russian Revolution</a> in 1917, the short-lived <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_People%27s_Republic" title="Ukrainian People&#39;s Republic">Ukrainian People's Republic</a> was formed. The <a href="/wiki/Bolsheviks" title="Bolsheviks">Bolsheviks</a> consolidated control over much of the former empire and established the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Soviet_Socialist_Republic" title="Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic">Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic</a>, which became a <a href="/wiki/Republics_of_the_Soviet_Union" title="Republics of the Soviet Union">constituent republic</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Soviet_Union" title="Soviet Union">Soviet Union</a> when it was formed in 1922. In the early 1930s, millions of Ukrainians died in the <a href="/wiki/Holodomor" title="Holodomor">Holodomor</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Causes_of_the_Holodomor" title="Causes of the Holodomor">human-made famine</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Reichskommissariat_Ukraine" title="Reichskommissariat Ukraine">German occupation</a> during <a href="/wiki/World_War_II_in_Ukraine" class="mw-redirect" title="World War II in Ukraine">World War II in Ukraine</a> was devastating: 7 million Ukrainian civilians were killed, including the <a href="/wiki/The_Holocaust_in_Ukraine" title="The Holocaust in Ukraine">majority of Ukrainian Jews</a>.
</p><p>Ukraine gained independence in 1991 as the <a href="/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union" title="Dissolution of the Soviet Union">Soviet Union dissolved</a>, and declared itself <a href="/wiki/Neutral_country" title="Neutral country">neutral</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-gska2.rada.gov.ua_15-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-gska2.rada.gov.ua-15">&#91;12&#93;</a></sup> A new <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Ukraine" title="Constitution of Ukraine">constitution</a> was adopted in 1996. A series of mass demonstrations, known as the <a href="/wiki/Euromaidan" title="Euromaidan">Euromaidan</a>, led to the establishment of a new government in 2014 after a <a href="/wiki/Revolution_of_Dignity" title="Revolution of Dignity">revolution</a>. Russia then unilaterally <a href="/wiki/Annexation_of_Crimea_by_the_Russian_Federation" title="Annexation of Crimea by the Russian Federation">annexed</a> Ukraine's <a href="/wiki/Crimea" title="Crimea">Crimean Peninsula</a>; and <a href="/wiki/2014_pro-Russian_unrest_in_Ukraine" title="2014 pro-Russian unrest in Ukraine">pro-Russian unrest</a> culminated in <a href="/wiki/War_in_Donbas_(2014%E2%80%932022)" title="War in Donbas (2014–2022)">a war in the Donbas</a> between Russian-backed separatists and government forces in eastern Ukraine. Since the outbreak of <a href="/wiki/Russo-Ukrainian_War" title="Russo-Ukrainian War">war with Russia</a>, Ukraine has continued to seek closer ties with the <a href="/wiki/Ukraine%E2%80%93United_States_relations" title="Ukraine–United States relations">United States</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ukraine%E2%80%93European_Union_relations" title="Ukraine–European Union relations">European Union</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Ukraine%E2%80%93NATO_relations" title="Ukraine–NATO relations">NATO</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:5_16-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:5-16">&#91;13&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:6_17-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:6-17">&#91;14&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-European_Commission_Trade_Ukraine_18-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-European_Commission_Trade_Ukraine-18">&#91;15&#93;</a></sup> Russia launched a <a href="/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" title="Russian invasion of Ukraine">full-scale invasion</a> of Ukraine in 2022.
</p><p>Ukraine is a <a href="/wiki/Unitary_state" title="Unitary state">unitary state</a> with a <a href="/wiki/Semi-presidential_republic" title="Semi-presidential republic">semi-presidential system</a>. A <a href="/wiki/Developing_country" title="Developing country">developing country</a>, it is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_sovereign_states_in_Europe_by_GDP_(nominal)_per_capita" title="List of sovereign states in Europe by GDP (nominal) per capita">poorest country in Europe</a> by nominal GDP per capita<sup id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-19">&#91;16&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Corruption_in_Ukraine" title="Corruption in Ukraine">corruption</a> remains a significant issue.<sup id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-20">&#91;17&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-21" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-21">&#91;18&#93;</a></sup> However, due to <a href="/wiki/Geography_of_Ukraine" title="Geography of Ukraine">its extensive fertile land</a>, pre-war Ukraine was <a href="/wiki/Economy_of_Ukraine" title="Economy of Ukraine">one of the largest grain exporters in the world</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-grain1_22-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-grain1-22">&#91;19&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-grain2_23-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-grain2-23">&#91;20&#93;</a></sup> It is a founding member of the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations" title="United Nations">United Nations</a>, as well as a member of the <a href="/wiki/Council_of_Europe" title="Council of Europe">Council of Europe</a>, the <a href="/wiki/World_Trade_Organization" title="World Trade Organization">World Trade Organization</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Organization_for_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe" title="Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe">OSCE</a>. It is <a href="/wiki/Accession_of_Ukraine_to_the_European_Union" title="Accession of Ukraine to the European Union">in the process</a> of joining the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a> and has submitted an application for NATO membership.<sup id="cite_ref-24" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-24">&#91;21&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r886046785">.mw-parser-output .toclimit-2 .toclevel-1 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-3 .toclevel-2 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-4 .toclevel-3 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-5 .toclevel-4 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-6 .toclevel-5 ul,.mw-parser-output .toclimit-7 .toclevel-6 ul{display:none}</style><div class="toclimit-3"><meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" /></div>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Etymology_and_orthography">Etymology and orthography</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Name_of_Ukraine" title="Name of Ukraine">Name of Ukraine</a></div>
<p>The name of Ukraine likely comes from the <a href="/wiki/Old_Slavic" class="mw-redirect" title="Old Slavic">old Slavic</a> term for 'borderland',<sup id="cite_ref-25" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-25">&#91;22&#93;</a></sup> as does the word <i><a href="/wiki/Krajina" title="Krajina">krajina</a></i>.
</p><p><span class="anchor" id="the_Ukraine"></span>In the <a href="/wiki/English-speaking_world" title="English-speaking world">English-speaking world</a> during most of the 20th century, Ukraine (whether independent or not) was referred to as "the Ukraine".<sup id="cite_ref-merriam-webster_26-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-merriam-webster-26">&#91;23&#93;</a></sup> This is because the word <i>ukraina</i> means 'borderland'<sup id="cite_ref-27" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-27">&#91;24&#93;</a></sup> so the <a href="/wiki/Article_(grammar)" title="Article (grammar)">definite article</a> would be natural in the English language; this is similar to <i><span title="Dutch-language text"><i lang="nl">Nederlanden</i></span></i>, which means 'low lands' and is rendered in English as "<i>the</i> <a href="/wiki/Netherlands" title="Netherlands">Netherlands</a>".<sup id="cite_ref-28" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-28">&#91;25&#93;</a></sup> However, since Ukraine's <a href="/wiki/Declaration_of_Independence_of_Ukraine" title="Declaration of Independence of Ukraine">declaration of independence</a> in 1991, this usage has become politicised and is now rarer, and <a href="/wiki/Style_guide" title="Style guide">style guides</a> advise against its use.<sup id="cite_ref-UKrW812991TU_29-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UKrW812991TU-29">&#91;26&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-30" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-30">&#91;27&#93;</a></sup> US ambassador <a href="/wiki/William_B._Taylor_Jr." title="William B. Taylor Jr.">William Taylor</a> said that using "the Ukraine" implies disregard for Ukrainian sovereignty.<sup id="cite_ref-31" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-31">&#91;28&#93;</a></sup> The official Ukrainian position is that "the Ukraine" is both grammatically and politically incorrect.<sup id="cite_ref-BBC_News_Magazine_32-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BBC_News_Magazine-32">&#91;29&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="History">History</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/History_of_Ukraine" title="History of Ukraine">History of Ukraine</a></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Early_history">Early history</span></h3>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Indo-European_migrations.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Indo-European_migrations.jpg/300px-Indo-European_migrations.jpg" decoding="async" width="300" height="124" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Indo-European_migrations.jpg/450px-Indo-European_migrations.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Indo-European_migrations.jpg/600px-Indo-European_migrations.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3326" data-file-height="1372" /></a><figcaption>Early <a href="/wiki/Indo-European_migrations" title="Indo-European migrations">Indo-European migrations</a> from the <a href="/wiki/Pontic_steppes" class="mw-redirect" title="Pontic steppes">Pontic steppes</a> of present-day Ukraine and Russia<sup id="cite_ref-33" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-33">&#91;30&#93;</a></sup></figcaption></figure>
<p>Settlement by <a href="/wiki/Modern_humans" class="mw-redirect" title="Modern humans">modern humans</a> in Ukraine and its vicinity dates back to 32,000 BC, with evidence of the <a href="/wiki/Gravettian_culture" class="mw-redirect" title="Gravettian culture">Gravettian culture</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Crimean_Mountains" title="Crimean Mountains">Crimean Mountains</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-orig_34-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-orig-34">&#91;31&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-bbc_35-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bbc-35">&#91;32&#93;</a></sup> By 4,500 BC, the <a href="/wiki/Neolithic" title="Neolithic">Neolithic</a> <a href="/wiki/Cucuteni%E2%80%93Trypillia_culture" title="Cucuteni–Trypillia culture">Cucuteni–Trypillia culture</a> was flourishing in wide areas of modern Ukraine, including <a href="/wiki/Trypillia" title="Trypillia">Trypillia</a> and the entire <a href="/wiki/Dnieper" title="Dnieper">Dnieper</a>-<a href="/wiki/Dniester" title="Dniester">Dniester</a> region. Ukraine is also considered to be the likely location of the first <a href="/wiki/Domestication_of_the_horse" title="Domestication of the horse">domestication of the horse</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-36" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-36">&#91;33&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-37" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-37">&#91;34&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-38" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-38">&#91;35&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-cbc.ca_39-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cbc.ca-39">&#91;36&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Kurgan_hypothesis" title="Kurgan hypothesis">Kurgan hypothesis</a> places the Volga-Dnieper region of Ukraine and southern Russia as the <a href="/wiki/Linguistic_homeland" title="Linguistic homeland">linguistic homeland</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Proto-Indo-Europeans" title="Proto-Indo-Europeans">Proto-Indo-Europeans</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-40" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-40">&#91;37&#93;</a></sup> Early <a href="/wiki/Indo-European_migrations" title="Indo-European migrations">Indo-European migrations</a> from the Pontic steppes in the 3rd millennium BC spread <a href="/wiki/Yamnaya_culture" title="Yamnaya culture">Yamnaya</a> <a href="/wiki/Western_Steppe_Herders" title="Western Steppe Herders">Steppe pastoralist</a> ancestry and <a href="/wiki/Indo-European_languages" title="Indo-European languages">Indo-European languages</a> across large parts of Europe.<sup id="cite_ref-41" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-41">&#91;38&#93;</a></sup> During the <a href="/wiki/Iron_Age" title="Iron Age">Iron Age</a>, the land was inhabited by <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Iranian_languages" title="Eastern Iranian languages">Iranian</a>-speaking <a href="/wiki/Cimmerians" title="Cimmerians">Cimmerians</a>, <a href="/wiki/Scythians" title="Scythians">Scythians</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Sarmatians" title="Sarmatians">Sarmatians</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-42" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-42">&#91;39&#93;</a></sup> Between 700&#160;BC and 200&#160;BC it was part of the <a href="/wiki/Scythia" title="Scythia">Scythian</a> kingdom.<sup id="cite_ref-43" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-43">&#91;40&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>From the 6th&#160;century BC, <a href="/wiki/Ancient_Greece" title="Ancient Greece">Greek</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ancient_Rome" title="Ancient Rome">Roman</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Byzantine_Empire" title="Byzantine Empire">Byzantine</a> colonies were established on the north-eastern shore of the <a href="/wiki/Black_Sea" title="Black Sea">Black Sea</a>, such as at <a href="/wiki/Tyras" title="Tyras">Tyras</a>, <a href="/wiki/Olbia,_Ukraine" class="mw-redirect" title="Olbia, Ukraine">Olbia</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Chersonesus" title="Chersonesus">Chersonesus</a>. These thrived into the 6th&#160;century AD. The <a href="/wiki/Goths" title="Goths">Goths</a> stayed in the area, but came under the sway of the <a href="/wiki/Huns" title="Huns">Huns</a> from the 370s. In the 7th&#160;century, the territory that is now eastern Ukraine was the centre of <a href="/wiki/Old_Great_Bulgaria" title="Old Great Bulgaria">Old Great Bulgaria</a>. At the end of the century, the majority of Bulgar tribes migrated in different directions, and the <a href="/wiki/Khazars" title="Khazars">Khazars</a> took over much of the land.<sup id="cite_ref-44" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-44">&#91;41&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In the 5th and 6th centuries, the <a href="/wiki/Early_Slavs" title="Early Slavs">early Slavic</a> <a href="/wiki/Antes_(people)" class="mw-redirect" title="Antes (people)">Antes people</a> lived in Ukraine. Migrations from the territories of present-day Ukraine throughout the <a href="/wiki/Balkans" title="Balkans">Balkans</a> established many <a href="/wiki/South_Slavs" title="South Slavs">South Slavic</a> nations. Northern migrations, reaching almost to <a href="/wiki/Lake_Ilmen" title="Lake Ilmen">Lake Ilmen</a>, led to the emergence of the <a href="/wiki/Ilmen_Slavs" class="mw-redirect" title="Ilmen Slavs">Ilmen Slavs</a> and <a href="/wiki/Krivichs" title="Krivichs">Krivichs</a>. Following an <a href="/wiki/Pannonian_Avars" title="Pannonian Avars">Avar</a> raid in 602 and the collapse of the Antes Union, most of these peoples survived as separate tribes until the beginning of the second millennium.<sup id="cite_ref-45" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-45">&#91;42&#93;</a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability" title="Wikipedia:Verifiability"><span title="Quotation needed from source to verify. (March 2022)">need quotation to verify</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Golden_Age_of_Kyiv">Golden Age of Kyiv</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Kievan_Rus%27" title="Kievan Rus&#39;">Kievan Rus'</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Principalities_of_Kievan_Rus%27_(1054-1132).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Principalities_of_Kievan_Rus%27_%281054-1132%29.jpg/260px-Principalities_of_Kievan_Rus%27_%281054-1132%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="260" height="347" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Principalities_of_Kievan_Rus%27_%281054-1132%29.jpg/390px-Principalities_of_Kievan_Rus%27_%281054-1132%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Principalities_of_Kievan_Rus%27_%281054-1132%29.jpg/520px-Principalities_of_Kievan_Rus%27_%281054-1132%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="770" data-file-height="1028" /></a><figcaption>The furthest extent of <a href="/wiki/Kievan_Rus%27" title="Kievan Rus&#39;">Kievan Rus'</a>, 1054–1132</figcaption></figure>
<p>The establishment of the state of <a href="/wiki/Kievan_Rus%27" title="Kievan Rus&#39;">Kievan Rus'</a> remains obscure and uncertain.<sup id="cite_ref-46" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-46">&#91;43&#93;</a></sup> The state included much of present-day Ukraine, <a href="/wiki/Belarus" title="Belarus">Belarus</a> and the western part of <a href="/wiki/European_Russia" title="European Russia">European Russia</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Columbia_47-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Columbia-47">&#91;44&#93;</a></sup> According to the <i><a href="/wiki/Primary_Chronicle" title="Primary Chronicle">Primary Chronicle</a></i>, the <a href="/wiki/Rus%27_people" title="Rus&#39; people">Rus' people</a> initially consisted of <a href="/wiki/Varangian" class="mw-redirect" title="Varangian">Varangians</a> from <a href="/wiki/Scandinavia" title="Scandinavia">Scandinavia</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-48" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-48">&#91;45&#93;</a></sup> In 882, the pagan <a href="/wiki/Oleg_of_Novgorod" class="mw-redirect" title="Oleg of Novgorod">Prince Oleg</a> (Oleh) conquered <a href="/wiki/Kyiv" title="Kyiv">Kyiv</a> from <a href="/wiki/Askold_and_Dir" title="Askold and Dir">Askold and Dir</a> and proclaimed it as the new capital of the Rus'.<sup id="cite_ref-49" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-49">&#91;46&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Anti-Normanism" title="Anti-Normanism">Anti-Normanist</a> historians however argue that the East Slavic tribes along the southern parts of the <a href="/wiki/Dnieper_River" class="mw-redirect" title="Dnieper River">Dnieper River</a> were already in the process of forming a state independently.<sup id="cite_ref-martin_50-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-martin-50">&#91;47&#93;</a></sup> The Varangian elite, including the ruling <a href="/wiki/Rurik_dynasty" class="mw-redirect" title="Rurik dynasty">Rurik dynasty</a>, later assimilated into the Slavic population.<sup id="cite_ref-Columbia_47-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Columbia-47">&#91;44&#93;</a></sup> Kievan Rus' was composed of several <a href="/wiki/Principality" title="Principality">principalities</a> ruled by the interrelated Rurikid <i><a href="/wiki/Knyaz" title="Knyaz">kniazes</a></i> ("princes"), who often fought each other for possession of Kyiv.<sup id="cite_ref-51" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-51">&#91;48&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>During the 10th and 11th&#160;centuries, Kievan Rus' became the largest and most powerful state in Europe, a period known as its Golden Age.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_52-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-52">&#91;49&#93;</a></sup> It began with the reign of <a href="/wiki/Vladimir_the_Great" title="Vladimir the Great">Vladimir the Great</a> (980–1015), who <a href="/wiki/Christianization_of_Kievan_Rus%27" title="Christianization of Kievan Rus&#39;">introduced Christianity</a>. During the reign of his son, <a href="/wiki/Yaroslav_the_Wise" title="Yaroslav the Wise">Yaroslav the Wise</a> (1019–1054), Kievan Rus' reached the zenith of its cultural development and military power.<sup id="cite_ref-Columbia_47-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Columbia-47">&#91;44&#93;</a></sup> The state soon fragmented as the relative importance of regional powers rose again. After a final resurgence under the rule of <a href="/wiki/Vladimir_II_Monomakh" title="Vladimir II Monomakh">Vladimir II Monomakh</a> (1113–1125) and his son <a href="/wiki/Mstislav_I_of_Kiev" title="Mstislav I of Kiev">Mstislav</a> (1125–1132), Kievan Rus' finally disintegrated into separate principalities following Mstislav's death, though ownership of Kyiv would still carry great prestige for decades.<sup id="cite_ref-53" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-53">&#91;50&#93;</a></sup> In the 11th and 12th centuries, the nomadic confederacy of the <a href="/wiki/Turkic_languages" title="Turkic languages">Turkic</a>-speaking <a href="/wiki/Cumans" title="Cumans">Cumans</a> and <a href="/wiki/Kipchaks" title="Kipchaks">Kipchaks</a> was the dominant force in the <a href="/wiki/Pontic_steppe" class="mw-redirect" title="Pontic steppe">Pontic steppe</a> north of the Black Sea.<sup id="cite_ref-54" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-54">&#91;51&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Mongol_invasion_of_Rus%27" class="mw-redirect" title="Mongol invasion of Rus&#39;">Mongol invasions</a> in the mid-13th century devastated Kievan Rus', and Kyiv was <a href="/wiki/Siege_of_Kyiv_(1240)" class="mw-redirect" title="Siege of Kyiv (1240)">completely destroyed</a> in 1240.<sup id="cite_ref-55" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-55">&#91;52&#93;</a></sup> In the western territories, the principalities of <a href="/wiki/Principality_of_Halych" title="Principality of Halych">Halych</a> and <a href="/wiki/Principality_of_Volhynia" title="Principality of Volhynia">Volhynia</a> had arisen earlier, and were merged to form the <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Galicia%E2%80%93Volhynia" title="Kingdom of Galicia–Volhynia">Principality of Galicia–Volhynia</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-56" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-56">&#91;53&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Daniel_of_Galicia" title="Daniel of Galicia">Daniel of Galicia</a>, son of <a href="/wiki/Roman_the_Great" title="Roman the Great">Roman the Great</a>, re-united much of south-western Rus', including <a href="/wiki/Volhynia" title="Volhynia">Volhynia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Galicia_(Eastern_Europe)" title="Galicia (Eastern Europe)">Galicia</a>, as well as Kyiv. He was subsequently crowned by a <a href="/wiki/Pope" title="Pope">papal</a> envoy as the first <a href="/wiki/King_of_Ruthenia" title="King of Ruthenia">king of Galicia–Volhynia</a> (also known as the Kingdom of <a href="/wiki/Ruthenia" title="Ruthenia">Ruthenia</a>) in 1253.<sup id="cite_ref-57" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-57">&#91;54&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Foreign_domination">Foreign domination</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Grand_Duchy_of_Lithuania" title="Grand Duchy of Lithuania">Grand Duchy of Lithuania</a>, <a href="/wiki/Crown_of_the_Kingdom_of_Poland" title="Crown of the Kingdom of Poland">Crown of the Kingdom of Poland</a>, <a href="/wiki/Crimean_Khanate" title="Crimean Khanate">Crimean Khanate</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman Empire</a>, <a href="/wiki/Polish%E2%80%93Lithuanian_Commonwealth" title="Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth">Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Russian_Empire" title="Russian Empire">Russian Empire</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Rzeczpospolita2nar.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f0/Rzeczpospolita2nar.png/220px-Rzeczpospolita2nar.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="156" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f0/Rzeczpospolita2nar.png/330px-Rzeczpospolita2nar.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f0/Rzeczpospolita2nar.png/440px-Rzeczpospolita2nar.png 2x" data-file-width="3507" data-file-height="2480" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Polish%E2%80%93Lithuanian_Commonwealth" title="Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth">Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth</a> at its maximum extent in 1619. <a href="/wiki/Poland" title="Poland">Poland</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Crown_of_the_Kingdom_of_Poland" title="Crown of the Kingdom of Poland">Polish Crown</a> exercised power over much of Ukraine after <a href="/wiki/Union_of_Lublin" title="Union of Lublin">1569</a>. <br /> <style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r981673959">.mw-parser-output .legend{page-break-inside:avoid;break-inside:avoid-column}.mw-parser-output .legend-color{display:inline-block;min-width:1.25em;height:1.25em;line-height:1.25;margin:1px 0;text-align:center;border:1px solid black;background-color:transparent;color:black}.mw-parser-output .legend-text{}</style><span class="legend nowrap"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:salmon; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Crown_of_the_Kingdom_of_Poland" title="Crown of the Kingdom of Poland">Crown of the Kingdom of Poland</a></span><br /> <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><span class="legend nowrap"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:hotpink; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Grand_Duchy_of_Lithuania" title="Grand Duchy of Lithuania">Grand Duchy of Lithuania</a></span><br /> <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><span class="legend nowrap"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:dimgrey; color:white;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Duchy_of_Livonia" title="Duchy of Livonia">Duchy of Livonia</a></span><br /> <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><span class="legend nowrap"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:lightgrey; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Duchy_of_Prussia" title="Duchy of Prussia">Duchy of Prussia</a>, Polish <a href="/wiki/Fief" title="Fief">fief</a></span><br /> <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><span class="legend nowrap"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:mediumorchid; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Duchy_of_Courland_and_Semigallia" title="Duchy of Courland and Semigallia">Duchy of Courland and Semigallia</a>, Commonwealth fief</span></figcaption></figure>
<p>In 1349, in the aftermath of the <a href="/wiki/Galicia%E2%80%93Volhynia_Wars" title="Galicia–Volhynia Wars">Galicia–Volhynia Wars</a>, the region was partitioned between the <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Poland" title="Kingdom of Poland">Kingdom of Poland</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Grand_Duchy_of_Lithuania" title="Grand Duchy of Lithuania">Grand Duchy of Lithuania</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-rowell266_58-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rowell266-58">&#91;55&#93;</a></sup> From the mid-13th century to the late 1400s, the <a href="/wiki/Republic_of_Genoa" title="Republic of Genoa">Republic of Genoa</a> founded numerous <a href="/wiki/Colonies" class="mw-redirect" title="Colonies">colonies</a> on the northern coast of the Black Sea and transformed these into large commercial centers headed by the consul, a representative of the Republic.<sup id="cite_ref-59" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-59">&#91;56&#93;</a></sup> In 1430, the region of <a href="/wiki/Podolia" title="Podolia">Podolia</a> was incorporated into Poland, and the lands of modern-day Ukraine became increasingly settled by <a href="/wiki/Polish_people" title="Polish people">Poles</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-60" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-60">&#91;57&#93;</a></sup> In 1441, <a href="/wiki/Genghisid" class="mw-redirect" title="Genghisid">Genghisid</a> prince <a href="/wiki/Haci_I_Giray" class="mw-redirect" title="Haci I Giray">Haci I Giray</a> founded the <a href="/wiki/Crimean_Khanate" title="Crimean Khanate">Crimean Khanate</a> on the <a href="/wiki/Crimean_Peninsula" class="mw-redirect" title="Crimean Peninsula">Crimean Peninsula</a> and the surrounding steppes;<sup id="cite_ref-61" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-61">&#91;58&#93;</a></sup> the Khanate orchestrated <a href="/wiki/Tatars" title="Tatars">Tatar</a> <a href="/wiki/Crimean%E2%80%93Nogai_slave_raids_in_Eastern_Europe" title="Crimean–Nogai slave raids in Eastern Europe">slave raids</a>. Over the next three centuries, they would enslave an estimated two million in the region.<sup id="cite_ref-62" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-62">&#91;59&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-63" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-63">&#91;60&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 1569, the <a href="/wiki/Union_of_Lublin" title="Union of Lublin">Union of Lublin</a> established the <a href="/wiki/Polish%E2%80%93Lithuanian_Commonwealth" title="Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth">Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth</a>, and most of the Ukrainian lands were transferred from Lithuania to the <a href="/wiki/Crown_of_the_Kingdom_of_Poland" title="Crown of the Kingdom of Poland">Crown of the Kingdom of Poland</a>, becoming <i><a href="/wiki/De_jure" title="De jure">de jure</a></i> Polish territory. Under the pressures of <a href="/wiki/Polonisation" class="mw-redirect" title="Polonisation">Polonisation</a>, many landed gentry of <a href="/wiki/Ruthenia" title="Ruthenia">Ruthenia</a> converted to <a href="/wiki/Roman_Catholicism" class="mw-redirect" title="Roman Catholicism">Catholicism</a> and joined the circles of the <a href="/wiki/Polish_nobility" class="mw-redirect" title="Polish nobility">Polish nobility</a>; others joined the newly created <a href="/wiki/Ruthenian_Uniate_Church" title="Ruthenian Uniate Church">Ruthenian Uniate Church</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-64" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-64">&#91;61&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Cossack_Hetmanate">Cossack Hetmanate</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Cossack_Hetmanate" title="Cossack Hetmanate">Cossack Hetmanate</a></div>
<p>Deprived of native protectors among the Ruthenian nobility, the peasants and townspeople began turning for protection to the emerging <a href="/wiki/Zaporozhian_Cossacks" title="Zaporozhian Cossacks">Zaporozhian Cossacks</a>. In the mid-17th&#160;century, a Cossack military quasi-state, the <a href="/wiki/Zaporozhian_Host" title="Zaporozhian Host">Zaporozhian Host</a>, was formed by <a href="/wiki/Dnieper_Cossacks" class="mw-redirect" title="Dnieper Cossacks">Dnieper Cossacks</a> and Ruthenian peasants.<sup id="cite_ref-zaporizhia_65-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-zaporizhia-65">&#91;62&#93;</a></sup> Poland exercised little real control over this population, but found the Cossacks to be useful against the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Turks</a> and <a href="/wiki/Crimean_Khanate" title="Crimean Khanate">Tatars</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-britcos_66-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-britcos-66">&#91;63&#93;</a></sup> and at times the two were allies in <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_wars_in_Europe" title="Ottoman wars in Europe">military campaigns</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-67" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-67">&#91;64&#93;</a></sup> However, the continued harsh <a href="/wiki/Serf" class="mw-redirect" title="Serf">enserfment</a> of Ruthenian peasantry by Polish <a href="/wiki/Szlachta" title="Szlachta">szlachta</a> (many of whom were Polonized <a href="/wiki/Ruthenian_nobility" title="Ruthenian nobility">Ruthenian nobles</a>) and the suppression of the Orthodox Church alienated the Cossacks.<sup id="cite_ref-britcos_66-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-britcos-66">&#91;63&#93;</a></sup> The latter did not shy from taking up arms against those they perceived as enemies and occupiers, including the Catholic Church with its local representatives.<sup id="cite_ref-68" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-68">&#91;65&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Hondius_Bohdan_Khmelnytsky.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/33/Hondius_Bohdan_Khmelnytsky.jpg/200px-Hondius_Bohdan_Khmelnytsky.jpg" decoding="async" width="200" height="277" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/33/Hondius_Bohdan_Khmelnytsky.jpg/300px-Hondius_Bohdan_Khmelnytsky.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/33/Hondius_Bohdan_Khmelnytsky.jpg/400px-Hondius_Bohdan_Khmelnytsky.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1082" data-file-height="1500" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Hetmans_of_Ukrainian_Cossacks" title="Hetmans of Ukrainian Cossacks">Hetman</a> <a href="/wiki/Bohdan_Khmelnytsky" title="Bohdan Khmelnytsky">Bohdan Khmelnytsky</a> established an independent <a href="/wiki/Cossack_Hetmanate" title="Cossack Hetmanate">Cossack state</a> after the <a href="/wiki/Khmelnytsky_Uprising" title="Khmelnytsky Uprising">1648 uprising</a> against Poland.</figcaption></figure>
<p>In 1648, <a href="/wiki/Bohdan_Khmelnytsky" title="Bohdan Khmelnytsky">Bohdan Khmelnytsky</a> led the <a href="/wiki/Khmelnytsky_Uprising" title="Khmelnytsky Uprising">largest of the Cossack uprisings</a> against the Commonwealth and the <a href="/wiki/List_of_Polish_monarchs" title="List of Polish monarchs">Polish king</a>, which enjoyed wide support from the local population.<sup id="cite_ref-69" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-69">&#91;66&#93;</a></sup> Khmelnytsky founded the <a href="/wiki/Cossack_Hetmanate" title="Cossack Hetmanate">Cossack Hetmanate</a>, which existed until 1764 (some sources claim until 1782).<sup id="cite_ref-70" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-70">&#91;67&#93;</a></sup> After Khmelnytsky suffered a crushing defeat at the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Berestechko" title="Battle of Berestechko">Battle of Berestechko</a> in 1651, he turned to the <a href="/wiki/List_of_Russian_monarchs" title="List of Russian monarchs">Russian tsar</a> for help. In 1654, Khmelnytsky was subject to the <a href="/wiki/Pereiaslav_Agreement" title="Pereiaslav Agreement">Pereiaslav Agreement</a>, forming a military and political alliance with Russia that acknowledged loyalty to the Russian monarch.
</p><p>After his death, the Hetmanate went through a devastating 30-year war amongst Russia, Poland, the <a href="/wiki/Crimean_Khanate" title="Crimean Khanate">Crimean Khanate</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman Empire</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Cossacks" title="Cossacks">Cossacks</a>, known as "<a href="/wiki/The_Ruin_(Ukrainian_history)" title="The Ruin (Ukrainian history)">The Ruin</a>" (1657–1686), for control of the Cossack Hetmanate. The <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Perpetual_Peace_(1686)" title="Treaty of Perpetual Peace (1686)">Treaty of Perpetual Peace</a> between Russia and Poland in 1686 divided the lands of the Cossack Hetmanate between them, reducing the portion over which Poland had claimed sovereignty to Ukraine west of the <a href="/wiki/Dnieper" title="Dnieper">Dnieper</a> river. In 1686, the <a href="/wiki/Metropolitanate_of_Kyiv" title="Metropolitanate of Kyiv">Metropolitanate of Kyiv</a> was <a href="/wiki/Annexation_of_the_Metropolitanate_of_Kyiv_by_the_Moscow_Patriarchate" title="Annexation of the Metropolitanate of Kyiv by the Moscow Patriarchate">annexed by the Moscow Patriarchate</a> through a synodal letter of the <a href="/wiki/Ecumenical_Patriarch_of_Constantinople" title="Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople">Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople</a> <a href="/wiki/Dionysius_IV_of_Constantinople" title="Dionysius IV of Constantinople">Dionysius IV</a>, thus placing the <a href="/wiki/Metropolitanate_of_Kyiv#Orthodox_Church_of_Ukraine" title="Metropolitanate of Kyiv">Metropolitanate of Kyiv</a> under the authority of <a href="/wiki/Moscow" title="Moscow">Moscow</a>. An attempt to reverse the decline was undertaken by Cossack Hetman <a href="/wiki/Ivan_Mazepa" title="Ivan Mazepa">Ivan Mazepa</a> (1639–1709), who ultimately defected to the <a href="/wiki/Sweden" title="Sweden">Swedes</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Great_Northern_War" title="Great Northern War">Great Northern War</a> (1700–1721) in a bid to get rid of Russian dependence,<sup id="cite_ref-Magocsi_71-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Magocsi-71">&#91;68&#93;</a></sup> but they were crushed in the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Poltava" title="Battle of Poltava">Battle of Poltava</a> (1709).<sup id="cite_ref-Magocsi_71-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Magocsi-71">&#91;68&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The Hetmanate's autonomy was severely restricted since Poltava. In the years 1764–1781, <a href="/wiki/Catherine_the_Great" title="Catherine the Great">Catherine the Great</a> incorporated much of <a href="/wiki/Central_Ukraine" title="Central Ukraine">Central Ukraine</a> into the <a href="/wiki/Russian_Empire" title="Russian Empire">Russian Empire</a>, abolishing the <a href="/wiki/Cossack_Hetmanate" title="Cossack Hetmanate">Cossack Hetmanate</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Zaporozhian_Sich" title="Zaporozhian Sich">Zaporozhian Sich</a>, and was one of the people responsible for the suppression of the last major Cossack uprising, the <a href="/wiki/Koliivshchyna" title="Koliivshchyna">Koliivshchyna</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-72" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-72">&#91;69&#93;</a></sup> After the <a href="/wiki/Annexation_of_Crimea_by_the_Russian_Empire" class="mw-redirect" title="Annexation of Crimea by the Russian Empire">annexation of Crimea by Russia</a> in 1783, the newly acquired lands, now called <a href="/wiki/Novorossiya" title="Novorossiya">Novorossiya</a>, were opened up to settlement by Russians.<sup id="cite_ref-73" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-73">&#91;70&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Tsarist_autocracy" title="Tsarist autocracy">tsarist autocracy</a> established a policy of <a href="/wiki/Russification" title="Russification">Russification</a>, suppressing the use of the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_language" title="Ukrainian language">Ukrainian language</a> and curtailing the Ukrainian national identity.<sup id="cite_ref-censor_74-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-censor-74">&#91;71&#93;</a></sup> The western part of present-day Ukraine was subsequently split between Russia and <a href="/wiki/Habsburg" class="mw-redirect" title="Habsburg">Habsburg</a>-ruled <a href="/wiki/Austrian_Empire" title="Austrian Empire">Austria</a> after the <a href="/wiki/Partitions_of_Poland" title="Partitions of Poland">fall</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Polish%E2%80%93Lithuanian_Commonwealth" title="Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth">Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth</a> in 1795.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="19th_and_early_20th_century">19th and early 20th century</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Southwestern_Krai" title="Southwestern Krai">Southwestern Krai</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kharkov_Governorate" title="Kharkov Governorate">Kharkov Governorate</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Chernigov_Governorate" class="mw-redirect" title="Chernigov Governorate">Chernigov Governorate</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Ukraine_during_World_War_I" title="Ukraine during World War I">Ukraine during World War I</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ukraine_after_the_Russian_Revolution" title="Ukraine after the Russian Revolution">Ukraine after the Russian Revolution</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_War_of_Independence" title="Ukrainian War of Independence">Ukrainian War of Independence</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian%E2%80%93Soviet_War" title="Ukrainian–Soviet War">Ukrainian–Soviet War</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Polish_troops_in_Kiev.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/Polish_troops_in_Kiev.jpg/220px-Polish_troops_in_Kiev.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="160" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/Polish_troops_in_Kiev.jpg/330px-Polish_troops_in_Kiev.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/Polish_troops_in_Kiev.jpg/440px-Polish_troops_in_Kiev.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1200" data-file-height="873" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Kiev_offensive_(1920)" title="Kiev offensive (1920)">Polish troops enter Kyiv</a> in May 1920 during the <a href="/wiki/Polish%E2%80%93Soviet_War" title="Polish–Soviet War">Polish–Soviet War</a>. Following the <a href="/wiki/Peace_of_Riga" class="mw-redirect" title="Peace of Riga">Peace of Riga</a> signed on 18 March 1921, Poland took control of modern-day western Ukraine while Soviets took control of eastern and central Ukraine.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The 19th century saw the rise of Ukrainian nationalism. With growing urbanization and modernization and a cultural trend toward <a href="/wiki/Romantic_nationalism" title="Romantic nationalism">romantic nationalism</a>, a Ukrainian <a href="/wiki/Intelligentsia" title="Intelligentsia">intelligentsia</a> committed to national rebirth and social justice emerged. The serf-turned-national-poet <a href="/wiki/Taras_Shevchenko" title="Taras Shevchenko">Taras Shevchenko</a> (1814–1861) and political theorist <a href="/wiki/Mykhailo_Drahomanov" title="Mykhailo Drahomanov">Mykhailo Drahomanov</a> (1841–1895) led the growing nationalist movement.<sup id="cite_ref-75" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-75">&#91;72&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-76" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-76">&#91;73&#93;</a></sup> While conditions for its development in Austrian <a href="/wiki/Galicia_(eastern_Europe)" class="mw-redirect" title="Galicia (eastern Europe)">Galicia</a> under the <a href="/wiki/Habsburgs" class="mw-redirect" title="Habsburgs">Habsburgs</a> were relatively lenient,<sup id="cite_ref-77" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-77">&#91;74&#93;</a></sup> the Russian part (known as <a href="/wiki/Little_Russia" title="Little Russia">Little Russia</a>) faced severe restrictions, going as far as <a href="/wiki/Ems_Ukaz" title="Ems Ukaz">banning virtually all books from being published in Ukrainian</a> in 1876.
</p><p>Ukraine, like the rest of the Russian Empire, joined the <a href="/wiki/Industrial_Revolution" title="Industrial Revolution">Industrial Revolution</a> <a href="/wiki/Industrialization_in_the_Russian_Empire" title="Industrialization in the Russian Empire">later</a> than most of Western Europe<sup id="cite_ref-78" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-78">&#91;75&#93;</a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability" title="Wikipedia:Verifiability"><span title="The material near this tag failed verification of its source citation(s). (December 2022)">failed verification</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> due to the maintenance of <a href="/wiki/Serfdom_in_Russia" title="Serfdom in Russia">serfdom</a> until 1861.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (December 2022)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> Other than near the newly discovered coal fields of the <a href="/wiki/Donbas" title="Donbas">Donbas</a>, and in some larger cities such as <a href="/wiki/Odesa" title="Odesa">Odesa</a> and Kyiv, Ukraine largely remained an agricultural and resource extraction economy.<sup id="cite_ref-79" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-79">&#91;76&#93;</a></sup> The Austrian part of Ukraine <a href="/wiki/Poverty_in_Austrian_Galicia" title="Poverty in Austrian Galicia">was particularly destitute</a>, which forced hundreds of thousands of peasants into emigration, who created the backbone of an extensive <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_diaspora" title="Ukrainian diaspora">Ukrainian diaspora</a> in countries such as <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Canadians" title="Ukrainian Canadians">Canada</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Americans" title="Ukrainian Americans">United States</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Brazilians" title="Ukrainian Brazilians">Brazil</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-80" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-80">&#91;77&#93;</a></sup> Some of the Ukrainians settled in the Far East, too. According to the <a href="/wiki/1897_census" class="mw-redirect" title="1897 census">1897 census</a>, there were 223,000 ethnic Ukrainians in <a href="/wiki/Siberia" title="Siberia">Siberia</a> and 102,000 in <a href="/wiki/Central_Asia" title="Central Asia">Central Asia</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-81" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-81">&#91;78&#93;</a></sup> An additional 1.6 million emigrated to the east in the ten years after the opening of the <a href="/wiki/Trans-Siberian_Railway" title="Trans-Siberian Railway">Trans-Siberian Railway</a> in 1906.<sup id="cite_ref-82" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-82">&#91;79&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Russian_Far_East" title="Russian Far East">Far Eastern</a> areas with an ethnic Ukrainian population became known as <a href="/wiki/Green_Ukraine" title="Green Ukraine">Green Ukraine</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-83" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-83">&#91;80&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Ukraine plunged into turmoil with the beginning of <a href="/wiki/World_War_I" title="World War I">World War I</a>, and fighting on Ukrainian soil persisted until late 1921. Initially, the Ukrainians were split between Austria-Hungary, fighting for the <a href="/wiki/Central_Powers" title="Central Powers">Central Powers</a>, though the vast majority served in the <a href="/wiki/Military_history_of_Imperial_Russia" class="mw-redirect" title="Military history of Imperial Russia">Imperial Russian Army</a>, which was part of the <a href="/wiki/Triple_Entente" title="Triple Entente">Triple Entente</a>, under Russia.<sup id="cite_ref-84" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-84">&#91;81&#93;</a></sup> As the Russian Empire collapsed, the conflict evolved into the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_War_of_Independence" title="Ukrainian War of Independence">Ukrainian War of Independence</a>, with Ukrainians fighting alongside, or against, the <a href="/wiki/Red_Army" title="Red Army">Red</a>, <a href="/wiki/White_Army" title="White Army">White</a>, <a href="/wiki/Makhnovshchina" title="Makhnovshchina">Black</a> and <a href="/wiki/Green_armies" title="Green armies">Green armies</a>, with the Poles, Hungarians (in <a href="/wiki/Transcarpathian_Rus%27" class="mw-redirect" title="Transcarpathian Rus&#39;">Transcarpathia</a>), and Germans also intervening at various times.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ukrainian_national_costumes_04.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Ukrainian_national_costumes_04.jpg/220px-Ukrainian_national_costumes_04.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Ukrainian_national_costumes_04.jpg/330px-Ukrainian_national_costumes_04.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Ukrainian_national_costumes_04.jpg/440px-Ukrainian_national_costumes_04.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4032" data-file-height="3024" /></a><figcaption>Youth in national Ukrainian dress during a ceremony commemorating the 22nd January 1919 "Act of Reunification of the Ukrainian People's Republic and the Western Ukrainian People's Republic", which is honored yearly across 22 cities of Ukraine.</figcaption></figure>
<p>An attempt to create an independent state, the left-leaning <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_People%27s_Republic" title="Ukrainian People&#39;s Republic">Ukrainian People's Republic</a> (UNR), was first announced by <a href="/wiki/Mykhailo_Hrushevsky" title="Mykhailo Hrushevsky">Mykhailo Hrushevsky</a>, but the period was plagued by an extremely unstable political and military environment. It was first deposed in a <a href="/wiki/Coup_d%27%C3%A9tat" title="Coup d&#39;état">coup d'état</a> led by <a href="/wiki/Pavlo_Skoropadskyi" title="Pavlo Skoropadskyi">Pavlo Skoropadskyi</a>, which yielded the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_State" title="Ukrainian State">Ukrainian State</a> under the German protectorate, and the attempt to restore the UNR under the <a href="/wiki/Directorate_of_Ukraine" title="Directorate of Ukraine">Directorate</a> ultimately failed as the Ukrainian army was regularly overrun by other forces. The short-lived <a href="/wiki/West_Ukrainian_People%27s_Republic" title="West Ukrainian People&#39;s Republic">West Ukrainian People's Republic</a> and <a href="/wiki/Hutsul_Republic" title="Hutsul Republic">Hutsul Republic</a> also failed to join the rest of Ukraine.<sup id="cite_ref-85" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-85">&#91;82&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The result of the conflict was a partial victory for the <a href="/wiki/Second_Polish_Republic" title="Second Polish Republic">Second Polish Republic</a>, which annexed the Western Ukrainian provinces, as well as a larger-scale victory for the pro-Soviet forces, which succeeded in dislodging the remaining factions and eventually established the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Soviet_Socialist_Republic" title="Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic">Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic</a> (Soviet Ukraine). Meanwhile, modern-day <a href="/wiki/Bukovina" title="Bukovina">Bukovina</a> was occupied by <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Romania" title="Kingdom of Romania">Romania</a> and <a href="/wiki/Carpathian_Ruthenia" title="Carpathian Ruthenia">Carpathian Ruthenia</a> was admitted to <a href="/wiki/First_Czechoslovak_Republic" title="First Czechoslovak Republic">Czechoslovakia</a> as an autonomous region.<sup id="cite_ref-86" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-86">&#91;83&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The conflict over Ukraine, a part of the broader <a href="/wiki/Russian_Civil_War" title="Russian Civil War">Russian Civil War</a>, devastated the whole of the former <a href="/wiki/Russian_Empire" title="Russian Empire">Russian Empire</a>, including eastern and central Ukraine. The fighting left over 1.5 million people dead and hundreds of thousands homeless in the former Russian Empire's territory. The eastern provinces were additionally impacted by a <a href="/wiki/Russian_famine_of_1921%E2%80%931922" title="Russian famine of 1921–1922">famine in 1921</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-87" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-87">&#91;84&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-88" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-88">&#91;85&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Inter-war_Soviet_Ukraine">Inter-war Soviet Ukraine</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Holodomor" title="Holodomor">Holodomor</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:GolodomorKharkiv.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/GolodomorKharkiv.jpg/220px-GolodomorKharkiv.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="164" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/GolodomorKharkiv.jpg/330px-GolodomorKharkiv.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/GolodomorKharkiv.jpg/440px-GolodomorKharkiv.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1600" data-file-height="1191" /></a><figcaption>Starved peasants on a street in <a href="/wiki/Kharkiv" title="Kharkiv">Kharkiv</a>, 1933. <a href="/wiki/Collectivization" class="mw-redirect" title="Collectivization">Collectivization</a> of crops and their confiscation by Soviet authorities led to a major famine in Soviet Ukraine known as the <a href="/wiki/Holodomor" title="Holodomor">Holodomor</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>In <a href="/wiki/Second_Polish_Republic" title="Second Polish Republic">Poland</a>, Marshal <a href="/wiki/J%C3%B3zef_Pi%C5%82sudski" title="Józef Piłsudski">Józef Piłsudski</a> and his political allies wanted to gain Ukrainian support by offering limited local autonomy as way to minimise Soviet influences in the borderlands.<sup id="cite_ref-89" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-89">&#91;86&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-90" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-90">&#91;87&#93;</a></sup> However, this approach was abandoned after Piłsudski's death in 1935, due to continued unrest among the Ukrainian population, with the Polish government responding by restricting rights of people who declared Ukrainian nationality and belonged to the <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Church" title="Eastern Orthodox Church">Eastern Orthodox Church</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-auto2_91-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto2-91">&#91;88&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-auto3_92-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto3-92">&#91;89&#93;</a></sup> In consequence, an underground Ukrainian nationalist and militant movement arose in the 1920s and 1930s, which gradually transformed into the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Military_Organization" title="Ukrainian Military Organization">Ukrainian Military Organization</a> and later the <a href="/wiki/Organisation_of_Ukrainian_Nationalists" title="Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists">Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists</a> (OUN).
</p><p>Meanwhile, the recently constituted Soviet Ukraine became one of the founding republics of the <a href="/wiki/Soviet_Union" title="Soviet Union">Soviet Union</a>. During the 1920s,<sup id="cite_ref-93" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-93">&#91;90&#93;</a></sup> under the Ukrainisation policy pursued by the national Communist leadership of <a href="/wiki/Mykola_Skrypnyk" title="Mykola Skrypnyk">Mykola Skrypnyk</a>, Soviet leadership at first encouraged a national renaissance in <a href="/wiki/Culture_of_Ukraine" title="Culture of Ukraine">Ukrainian culture</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_language" title="Ukrainian language">language</a>. <a href="/wiki/Ukrainisation" class="mw-redirect" title="Ukrainisation">Ukrainisation</a> was part of the Soviet-wide policy of <a href="/wiki/Korenisation" class="mw-redirect" title="Korenisation">Korenisation</a> (literally <i>indigenisation</i>), which was intended to promote the advancement of native peoples, their language and culture into the governance of their respective republics.
</p><p>Around the same time, Soviet leader <a href="/wiki/Vladimir_Lenin" title="Vladimir Lenin">Vladimir Lenin</a> instituted the <a href="/wiki/New_Economic_Policy" title="New Economic Policy">New Economic Policy</a> (NEP), which introduced a form of <a href="/wiki/Market_socialism" title="Market socialism">market socialism</a>, allowing some private ownership of small and medium-sized productive enterprises, hoping to reconstruct the post-war Soviet Union that had been devastated by both WWI and later the civil war. The NEP was successful at restoring the formerly war-torn nation to pre-WWI levels of production and agricultural output by the mid-1920s, much of the latter based in Ukraine.<sup id="cite_ref-Service_94-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Service-94">&#91;91&#93;</a></sup> These policies attracted many prominent former UNR figures, including former UNR leader Hrushevsky, to return to Soviet Ukraine, where they were accepted, and participated in the advancement of Ukrainian science and culture.<sup id="cite_ref-95" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-95">&#91;92&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>This period was cut short when <a href="/wiki/Joseph_Stalin" title="Joseph Stalin">Joseph Stalin</a> became the leader of the USSR following Lenin's death. Stalin did away with the NEP in what became known as the <a href="/wiki/Great_Break_(USSR)" title="Great Break (USSR)">Great Break</a>. Starting from the late 1920s and now with a <a href="/wiki/Planned_economy" title="Planned economy">centrally planned economy</a>, Soviet Ukraine took part in an <a href="/wiki/Industrialization_in_the_USSR" class="mw-redirect" title="Industrialization in the USSR">industrialisation scheme</a> which quadrupled its industrial output during the 1930s.
</p><p>However, as a consequence of Stalin's new policy, the Ukrainian peasantry suffered from the <a href="/wiki/Collectivization_in_the_USSR" class="mw-redirect" title="Collectivization in the USSR">programme of collectivization</a> of agricultural crops. Collectivization was part of the <a href="/wiki/First_five-year_plan" title="First five-year plan">first five-year plan</a> and was enforced by regular troops and the secret police known as <a href="/wiki/Cheka" title="Cheka">Cheka</a>. Those who resisted were <a href="/wiki/Population_transfer_in_the_Soviet_Union" title="Population transfer in the Soviet Union">arrested and deported</a> to <a href="/wiki/Gulag" title="Gulag">gulags</a> and work camps. As members of the collective farms were sometimes not allowed to receive any grain until unrealistic quotas were met, millions starved to death in a <a href="/wiki/Droughts_and_famines_in_Russia_and_the_Soviet_Union" title="Droughts and famines in Russia and the Soviet Union">famine</a> known as the <a href="/wiki/Holodomor" title="Holodomor">Holodomor</a> or the "Great Famine", which was recognized by some countries as an act of <a href="/wiki/Genocide" title="Genocide">genocide</a> perpetrated by <a href="/wiki/Joseph_Stalin" title="Joseph Stalin">Joseph Stalin</a> and other Soviet notables.<sup id="cite_ref-96" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-96">&#91;93&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Following on the Russian Civil War, and collectivisation, the <a href="/wiki/Great_Purge" title="Great Purge">Great Purge</a>, while killing Stalin's perceived political enemies, resulted in a profound loss of a new generation of Ukrainian <a href="/wiki/Intelligentsia" title="Intelligentsia">intelligentsia</a>, known today as the <a href="/wiki/Executed_Renaissance" title="Executed Renaissance">Executed Renaissance</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-97" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-97">&#91;94&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="World_War_II">World War II</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Front_(World_War_II)" title="Eastern Front (World War II)">Eastern Front (World War II)</a>, <a href="/wiki/Reichskommissariat_Ukraine" title="Reichskommissariat Ukraine">Reichskommissariat Ukraine</a>, and <a href="/wiki/The_Holocaust_in_Ukraine" title="The Holocaust in Ukraine">The Holocaust in Ukraine</a></div>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ukraine-growth.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/Ukraine-growth.png/300px-Ukraine-growth.png" decoding="async" width="300" height="178" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/Ukraine-growth.png/450px-Ukraine-growth.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/Ukraine-growth.png/600px-Ukraine-growth.png 2x" data-file-width="800" data-file-height="475" /></a><figcaption>Territorial evolution of the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_SSR" class="mw-redirect" title="Ukrainian SSR">Ukrainian SSR</a>, 1922–1954<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (February 2023)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup></figcaption></figure>
<p>Following the <a href="/wiki/Invasion_of_Poland" title="Invasion of Poland">Invasion of Poland</a> in September 1939, <a href="/wiki/Nazi_Germany" title="Nazi Germany">German</a> and <a href="/wiki/Soviet_Army" title="Soviet Army">Soviet</a> troops divided the territory of Poland. Thus, Eastern <a href="/wiki/Galicia_(Eastern_Europe)" title="Galicia (Eastern Europe)">Galicia</a> and <a href="/wiki/Volhynia" title="Volhynia">Volhynia</a> with their Ukrainian population became part of Ukraine. For the first time in history, the nation was united.<sup id="cite_ref-98" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-98">&#91;95&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-99" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-99">&#91;96&#93;</a></sup> Further territorial gains were secured in 1940, when the Ukrainian SSR incorporated the northern and southern districts of <a href="/wiki/Bessarabia" title="Bessarabia">Bessarabia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Northern_Bukovina" class="mw-redirect" title="Northern Bukovina">Northern Bukovina</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Hertsa_region" title="Hertsa region">Hertsa region</a> from the territories the USSR <a href="/wiki/Soviet_occupation_of_Bessarabia_and_Northern_Bukovina" title="Soviet occupation of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina">forced Romania to cede</a>, though it handed over the western part of the <a href="/wiki/Moldavian_Autonomous_Soviet_Socialist_Republic" title="Moldavian Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic">Moldavian Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic</a> to the newly created <a href="/wiki/Moldavian_SSR" class="mw-redirect" title="Moldavian SSR">Moldavian SSR</a>. These territorial gains of the USSR were internationally recognized by the <a href="/wiki/Paris_Peace_Treaties,_1947" title="Paris Peace Treaties, 1947">Paris peace treaties of 1947</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-100" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-100">&#91;97&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:%D0%9C%D0%B0%D1%80%D1%88%D0%B0%D0%BB_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D1%8E%D0%B7%D0%B0_%D0%93%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B9_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D1%8E%D0%B7%D0%B0_%D0%A1%D0%B5%D0%BC%D1%91%D0%BD_%D0%9A%D0%BE%D0%BD%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D1%82%D0%B8%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87_%D0%A2%D0%B8%D0%BC%D0%BE%D1%88%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%BA%D0%BE.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img
