decoding="async" width="220" height="297" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fe/%D0%9C%D0%B0%D1%80%D1%88%D0%B0%D0%BB_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D1%8E%D0%B7%D0%B0_%D0%93%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B9_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D1%8E%D0%B7%D0%B0_%D0%A1%D0%B5%D0%BC%D1%91%D0%BD_%D0%9A%D0%BE%D0%BD%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D1%82%D0%B8%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87_%D0%A2%D0%B8%D0%BC%D0%BE%D1%88%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%BA%D0%BE.jpg/330px-%D0%9C%D0%B0%D1%80%D1%88%D0%B0%D0%BB_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D1%8E%D0%B7%D0%B0_%D0%93%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B9_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D1%8E%D0%B7%D0%B0_%D0%A1%D0%B5%D0%BC%D1%91%D0%BD_%D0%9A%D0%BE%D0%BD%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D1%82%D0%B8%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87_%D0%A2%D0%B8%D0%BC%D0%BE%D1%88%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%BA%D0%BE.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fe/%D0%9C%D0%B0%D1%80%D1%88%D0%B0%D0%BB_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D1%8E%D0%B7%D0%B0_%D0%93%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B9_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D1%8E%D0%B7%D0%B0_%D0%A1%D0%B5%D0%BC%D1%91%D0%BD_%D0%9A%D0%BE%D0%BD%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D1%82%D0%B8%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87_%D0%A2%D0%B8%D0%BC%D0%BE%D1%88%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%BA%D0%BE.jpg/440px-%D0%9C%D0%B0%D1%80%D1%88%D0%B0%D0%BB_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D1%8E%D0%B7%D0%B0_%D0%93%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B9_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE_%D0%A1%D0%BE%D1%8E%D0%B7%D0%B0_%D0%A1%D0%B5%D0%BC%D1%91%D0%BD_%D0%9A%D0%BE%D0%BD%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D1%82%D0%B8%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87_%D0%A2%D0%B8%D0%BC%D0%BE%D1%88%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%BA%D0%BE.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1553" data-file-height="2096" /></a><figcaption>Marshal <a href="/wiki/Semyon_Timoshenko" title="Semyon Timoshenko">Semyon Timoshenko</a> (born in the <a href="/wiki/Budjak" title="Budjak">Budjak</a> region) commanded numerous fronts throughout the war, including the <a href="/wiki/Southwestern_Front_(Soviet_Union)" title="Southwestern Front (Soviet Union)">Southwestern Front</a> east of Kyiv in 1941.</figcaption></figure>
<p><a href="/wiki/Wehrmacht" title="Wehrmacht">German armies</a> <a href="/wiki/Operation_Barbarossa" title="Operation Barbarossa">invaded the Soviet Union</a> on 22 June 1941, initiating nearly four years of <a href="/wiki/Total_war" title="Total war">total war</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Axis_Powers" class="mw-redirect" title="Axis Powers">Axis</a> initially advanced against desperate but unsuccessful efforts of the <a href="/wiki/Red_Army" title="Red Army">Red Army</a>. In the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Kyiv_(1941)" class="mw-redirect" title="Battle of Kyiv (1941)">battle of Kyiv</a>, the city was acclaimed as a "<a href="/wiki/Hero_City_(Soviet_Union)" title="Hero City (Soviet Union)">Hero City</a>", because of its fierce <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Kyiv_(1941)" class="mw-redirect" title="Battle of Kyiv (1941)">resistance</a>. More than 600,000 Soviet soldiers (or one-quarter of the <a href="/wiki/Soviet_Western_Front" class="mw-redirect" title="Soviet Western Front">Soviet Western Front</a>) were killed or taken captive there, with many suffering <a href="/wiki/German_mistreatment_of_Soviet_prisoners_of_war" class="mw-redirect" title="German mistreatment of Soviet prisoners of war">severe mistreatment</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-101" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-101">&#91;98&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-102" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-102">&#91;99&#93;</a></sup> After its conquest, most of the Ukrainian SSR was organised within the <a href="/wiki/Reichskommissariat_Ukraine" title="Reichskommissariat Ukraine">Reichskommissariat Ukraine</a>, with the intention of exploiting its resources and eventual German settlement. Some western Ukrainians, who had only joined the Soviet Union in 1939, hailed the Germans as liberators, but that did not last long as the Nazis made little attempt to exploit dissatisfaction with Stalinist policies.<sup id="cite_ref-ww2_103-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ww2-103">&#91;100&#93;</a></sup> Instead, the Nazis preserved the collective-farm system, carried out <a href="/wiki/Mass_graves_in_the_Soviet_Union" class="mw-redirect" title="Mass graves in the Soviet Union">genocidal policies</a> against <a href="/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Ukraine" title="History of the Jews in Ukraine">Jews</a>, <a href="/wiki/OST-Arbeiter" class="mw-redirect" title="OST-Arbeiter">deported millions of people to work in Germany</a>, and began a depopulation program to prepare for German colonisation.<sup id="cite_ref-ww2_103-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ww2-103">&#91;100&#93;</a></sup> They blockaded the transport of food on the Dnieper River.<sup id="cite_ref-104" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-104">&#91;101&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Although the majority of Ukrainians fought in or alongside the Red Army and <a href="/wiki/Soviet_partisans" title="Soviet partisans">Soviet resistance</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-worldwars_105-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-worldwars-105">&#91;102&#93;</a></sup> in Western Ukraine an independent <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Insurgent_Army" title="Ukrainian Insurgent Army">Ukrainian Insurgent Army</a> movement arose (UPA, 1942). It was created as the armed forces of the underground <a href="/wiki/Organization_of_Ukrainian_Nationalists" class="mw-redirect" title="Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists">Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists</a> (OUN).<sup id="cite_ref-106" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-106">&#91;103&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-vedeneyev_107-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-vedeneyev-107">&#91;104&#93;</a></sup> Both organizations, the OUN and the UPA, supported the goal of an <a href="/wiki/Declaration_of_Ukrainian_Independence,_1941" class="mw-redirect" title="Declaration of Ukrainian Independence, 1941">independent Ukrainian state</a> on the territory with a Ukrainian ethnic majority. Although this brought conflict with Nazi Germany, at times the <a href="/wiki/Andriy_Atanasovych_Melnyk" class="mw-redirect" title="Andriy Atanasovych Melnyk">Melnyk</a> wing of the OUN allied with the Nazi forces. From mid-1943 until the end of the war, the UPA carried out <a href="/wiki/Massacres_of_Poles_in_Volhynia_and_Eastern_Galicia" title="Massacres of Poles in Volhynia and Eastern Galicia">massacres of ethnic Poles</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Volhynia" title="Volhynia">Volhynia</a> and <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Galicia" title="Eastern Galicia">Eastern Galicia</a> regions, killing around 100,000 Polish civilians, which brought reprisals.<sup id="cite_ref-108" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-108">&#91;105&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-IPNconf_109-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-IPNconf-109">&#91;106&#93;</a></sup> These organized massacres were an attempt by the OUN to create a homogeneous Ukrainian state without a Polish minority living within its borders, and to prevent the post-war Polish state from asserting its sovereignty over areas that had been part of pre-war Poland.<sup id="cite_ref-110" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-110">&#91;107&#93;</a></sup> After the war, the UPA continued to fight the USSR until the 1950s.<sup id="cite_ref-111" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-111">&#91;108&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-112" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-112">&#91;109&#93;</a></sup> At the same time, the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Liberation_Army" title="Ukrainian Liberation Army">Ukrainian Liberation Army</a>, another nationalist movement, fought alongside the Nazis.<sup id="cite_ref-Kalb2015_113-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Kalb2015-113">&#91;110&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ruined_Kiev_in_WWII.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/Ruined_Kiev_in_WWII.jpg/220px-Ruined_Kiev_in_WWII.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="140" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/Ruined_Kiev_in_WWII.jpg/330px-Ruined_Kiev_in_WWII.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/Ruined_Kiev_in_WWII.jpg/440px-Ruined_Kiev_in_WWII.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1925" data-file-height="1223" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Kyiv" title="Kyiv">Kyiv</a> suffered significant damage during <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Front_(World_War_II)" title="Eastern Front (World War II)">World War II</a>, and was occupied by the <a href="/wiki/Wehrmacht" title="Wehrmacht">Germans</a> from 19 September 1941 until 6 November 1943.</figcaption></figure>
<p>In total, the number of ethnic Ukrainians who fought in the ranks of the Soviet Army is estimated from 4.5&#160;million<sup id="cite_ref-worldwars_105-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-worldwars-105">&#91;102&#93;</a></sup> to 7&#160;million;<sup id="cite_ref-114" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-114">&#91;111&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-fn1_115-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fn1-115">&#91;d&#93;</a></sup> half of the <a href="/wiki/Soviet_Partisans" class="mw-redirect" title="Soviet Partisans">Pro-Soviet partisan</a> guerrilla resistance units, which counted up to 500,000 troops in 1944, were also Ukrainian.<sup id="cite_ref-116" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-116">&#91;112&#93;</a></sup> Generally, the Ukrainian Insurgent Army's figures are unreliable, with figures ranging anywhere from 15,000 to as many as 100,000 fighters.<sup id="cite_ref-117" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-117">&#91;113&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-118" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-118">&#91;114&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The vast majority of the fighting in World War II took place on the <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Front_(World_War_II)" title="Eastern Front (World War II)">Eastern Front</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-119" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-119">&#91;115&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/World_War_II_casualties_of_the_Soviet_Union" title="World War II casualties of the Soviet Union">total losses</a> inflicted upon the Ukrainian population during the war are estimated at 6 million,<sup id="cite_ref-120" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-120">&#91;116&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-dt-kul-dem-los_121-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dt-kul-dem-los-121">&#91;117&#93;</a></sup> including an estimated one and a half million Jews killed by the <a href="/wiki/Einsatzgruppen" title="Einsatzgruppen">Einsatzgruppen</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-122" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-122">&#91;118&#93;</a></sup> sometimes with the help of local collaborators. Of the estimated 8.6 million Soviet troop losses,<sup id="cite_ref-peremoga7_123-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-peremoga7-123">&#91;119&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-124" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-124">&#91;120&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Krivosheev_125-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Krivosheev-125">&#91;121&#93;</a></sup> 1.4&#160;million were ethnic <a href="/wiki/Ukrainians" title="Ukrainians">Ukrainians</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-peremoga7_123-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-peremoga7-123">&#91;119&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Krivosheev_125-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Krivosheev-125">&#91;121&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-fn1_115-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fn1-115">&#91;d&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-126" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-126">&#91;e&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Victory_Day_over_Nazism_in_World_War_II" title="Victory Day over Nazism in World War II">Victory Day</a> is celebrated as one of eleven Ukrainian national holidays.<sup id="cite_ref-127" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-127">&#91;122&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span id="Post.E2.80.93war_Soviet_Ukraine"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Post–war_Soviet_Ukraine">Post–war Soviet Ukraine</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Soviet_Socialist_Republic" title="Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic">Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic</a>, <a href="/wiki/History_of_the_Soviet_Union_(1953%E2%80%931964)" title="History of the Soviet Union (1953–1964)">History of the Soviet Union (1953–1964)</a>, <a href="/wiki/History_of_the_Soviet_Union_(1964%E2%80%931982)" title="History of the Soviet Union (1964–1982)">History of the Soviet Union (1964–1982)</a>, <a href="/wiki/History_of_the_Soviet_Union_(1982%E2%80%931991)" title="History of the Soviet Union (1982–1991)">History of the Soviet Union (1982–1991)</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Chernobyl_disaster" title="Chernobyl disaster">Chernobyl disaster</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Khrushchev_and_Brezhnev.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/c/c8/Khrushchev_and_Brezhnev.jpg/170px-Khrushchev_and_Brezhnev.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="295" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/c/c8/Khrushchev_and_Brezhnev.jpg/255px-Khrushchev_and_Brezhnev.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/c/c8/Khrushchev_and_Brezhnev.jpg/340px-Khrushchev_and_Brezhnev.jpg 2x" data-file-width="432" data-file-height="750" /></a><figcaption>Two future leaders of the <a href="/wiki/Soviet_Union" title="Soviet Union">Soviet Union</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev" title="Nikita Khrushchev">Nikita Khrushchev</a> (left, pre-war <a href="/wiki/Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union" title="Communist Party of the Soviet Union">CPSU</a> chief in Ukraine) and <a href="/wiki/Leonid_Brezhnev" title="Leonid Brezhnev">Leonid Brezhnev</a> (an engineer from <a href="/wiki/Kamianske" title="Kamianske">Kamianske</a>, Ukraine)</figcaption></figure>
<p>The republic was heavily damaged by the war, and it required significant efforts to recover. More than 700 cities and towns and 28,000 villages were destroyed.<sup id="cite_ref-128" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-128">&#91;123&#93;</a></sup> The situation was worsened by a <a href="/wiki/Famine" title="Famine">famine</a> in 1946–1947, which was caused by a drought and the wartime destruction of infrastructure, killing at least tens of thousands of people.<sup id="cite_ref-dt-kul-dem-los_121-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dt-kul-dem-los-121">&#91;117&#93;</a></sup> In 1945, the Ukrainian SSR became one of the founding members of the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations" title="United Nations">United Nations</a> (UN),<sup id="cite_ref-un_ukssr_129-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-un_ukssr-129">&#91;124&#93;</a></sup> part of a special agreement at the <a href="/wiki/Yalta_Conference" title="Yalta Conference">Yalta Conference</a>, and, alongside Belarus, had voting rights in the UN even though they were not independent.<sup id="cite_ref-130" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-130">&#91;125&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-131" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-131">&#91;126&#93;</a></sup> Moreover, Ukraine once more expanded its borders as it annexed <a href="/wiki/Zakarpattia_Oblast" title="Zakarpattia Oblast">Zakarpattia</a>, and the population became much more homogenized due to post-war <a href="/wiki/Population_transfer_in_the_Soviet_Union" title="Population transfer in the Soviet Union">population transfers</a>, most of which, as in the case of <a href="/wiki/Flight_and_expulsion_of_Germans_(1944%E2%80%931950)" class="mw-redirect" title="Flight and expulsion of Germans (1944–1950)">Germans</a> and <a href="/wiki/Deportation_of_the_Crimean_Tatars" title="Deportation of the Crimean Tatars">Crimean Tatars</a>, were forced. As of 1 January 1953, Ukrainians were second only to Russians among adult "<a href="/wiki/Forced_settlements_in_the_Soviet_Union" class="mw-redirect" title="Forced settlements in the Soviet Union">special deportees</a>", comprising 20% of the total.<sup id="cite_ref-Malynovska_132-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Malynovska-132">&#91;127&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Following the death of Stalin in 1953, <a href="/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev" title="Nikita Khrushchev">Nikita Khrushchev</a> became the new leader of the USSR, who began the policies of <a href="/wiki/De-Stalinization" title="De-Stalinization">De-Stalinization</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Khrushchev_Thaw" title="Khrushchev Thaw">Khrushchev Thaw</a>. During his term as head of the Soviet Union, <a href="/wiki/Crimean_Oblast" class="mw-redirect" title="Crimean Oblast">Crimea</a> was <a href="/wiki/1954_transfer_of_Crimea" class="mw-redirect" title="1954 transfer of Crimea">transferred</a> from the <a href="/wiki/Russian_SFSR" class="mw-redirect" title="Russian SFSR">Russian SFSR</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_SSR" class="mw-redirect" title="Ukrainian SSR">Ukrainian SSR</a>, formally as a friendship gift to Ukraine and for economic reasons.<sup id="cite_ref-133" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-133">&#91;128&#93;</a></sup> This represented the final extension of Ukrainian territory and formed the basis for the internationally recognized borders of Ukraine to this day. Ukraine was one of the most important republics of the Soviet Union, which resulted in many top positions in the Soviet Union being occupied by Ukrainians, including notably <a href="/wiki/Leonid_Brezhnev" title="Leonid Brezhnev">Leonid Brezhnev</a>, <a href="/wiki/General_Secretary_of_the_Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union" title="General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union">General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union</a> from 1964 to 1982. However, it was he and his <a href="/wiki/Communist_Party_of_Ukraine_(Soviet_Union)" title="Communist Party of Ukraine (Soviet Union)">appointee in Ukraine</a>, <a href="/wiki/Volodymyr_Shcherbytsky" title="Volodymyr Shcherbytsky">Volodymyr Shcherbytsky</a>, who presided over the extensive <a href="/wiki/Russification_of_Ukraine" title="Russification of Ukraine">Russification</a> of Ukraine and who were instrumental in repressing a new generation of Ukrainian intellectuals known as the <a href="/wiki/Sixtiers" title="Sixtiers">Sixtiers</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-134" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-134">&#91;129&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>By 1950, the republic had fully surpassed pre-war levels of industry and production.<sup id="cite_ref-135" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-135">&#91;130&#93;</a></sup> Soviet Ukraine soon became a European leader in industrial production<sup id="cite_ref-136" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-136">&#91;131&#93;</a></sup> and an important centre of the Soviet <a href="/wiki/Arms_industry" title="Arms industry">arms industry</a> and high-tech research, though heavy industry still had an outsided influence.<sup id="cite_ref-137" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-137">&#91;132&#93;</a></sup> The Soviet government invested in hydroelectric and nuclear power projects to cater to the energy demand that the development carried. On 26 April 1986, however, a reactor in the <a href="/wiki/Chernobyl_Nuclear_Power_Plant" title="Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant">Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant</a> exploded, resulting in the <a href="/wiki/Chernobyl_disaster" title="Chernobyl disaster">Chernobyl disaster</a>, the worst <a href="/wiki/Nuclear_reactor" title="Nuclear reactor">nuclear reactor</a> accident in history.<sup id="cite_ref-138" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-138">&#91;133&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Independence">Independence</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Modern_history_of_Ukraine" title="Modern history of Ukraine">Modern history of Ukraine</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union" title="Dissolution of the Soviet Union">Dissolution of the Soviet Union</a>, <a href="/wiki/Orange_Revolution" title="Orange Revolution">Orange Revolution</a>, <a href="/wiki/Revolution_of_Dignity" title="Revolution of Dignity">Revolution of Dignity</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Russo-Ukrainian_War" title="Russo-Ukrainian War">Russo-Ukrainian War</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:RIAN_archive_848095_Signing_the_Agreement_to_eliminate_the_USSR_and_establish_the_Commonwealth_of_Independent_States.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/RIAN_archive_848095_Signing_the_Agreement_to_eliminate_the_USSR_and_establish_the_Commonwealth_of_Independent_States.jpg/220px-RIAN_archive_848095_Signing_the_Agreement_to_eliminate_the_USSR_and_establish_the_Commonwealth_of_Independent_States.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/RIAN_archive_848095_Signing_the_Agreement_to_eliminate_the_USSR_and_establish_the_Commonwealth_of_Independent_States.jpg/330px-RIAN_archive_848095_Signing_the_Agreement_to_eliminate_the_USSR_and_establish_the_Commonwealth_of_Independent_States.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/RIAN_archive_848095_Signing_the_Agreement_to_eliminate_the_USSR_and_establish_the_Commonwealth_of_Independent_States.jpg/440px-RIAN_archive_848095_Signing_the_Agreement_to_eliminate_the_USSR_and_establish_the_Commonwealth_of_Independent_States.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1500" data-file-height="1000" /></a><figcaption>Ukrainian President <a href="/wiki/Leonid_Kravchuk" title="Leonid Kravchuk">Leonid Kravchuk</a> and Russian President <a href="/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin" title="Boris Yeltsin">Boris Yeltsin</a> signing the <a href="/wiki/Belavezha_Accords" class="mw-redirect" title="Belavezha Accords">Belavezha Accords</a>, which <a href="/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union" title="Dissolution of the Soviet Union">dissolved the Soviet Union</a>, on 8 December 1991</figcaption></figure>
<p><a href="/wiki/Mikhail_Gorbachev" title="Mikhail Gorbachev">Mikhail Gorbachev</a> pursued a policy of limited liberalization of public life, known as <i><a href="/wiki/Perestroika" title="Perestroika">perestroika</a>,</i> and attempted to reform a <a href="/wiki/Era_of_Stagnation" title="Era of Stagnation">stagnating economy</a>. The latter failed, but the democratization of the Soviet Union fuelled nationalist and separatist tendencies among the ethnic minorities, including Ukrainians.<sup id="cite_ref-139" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-139">&#91;134&#93;</a></sup> As part of the so-called <a href="/wiki/Parade_of_sovereignties" title="Parade of sovereignties">parade of sovereignties</a>, on 16 July 1990, the newly elected <a href="/wiki/Supreme_Soviet_of_the_Ukrainian_Soviet_Socialist_Republic" title="Supreme Soviet of the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic">Supreme Soviet of the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic</a> adopted the <a href="/wiki/Declaration_of_State_Sovereignty_of_Ukraine" title="Declaration of State Sovereignty of Ukraine">Declaration of State Sovereignty of Ukraine</a>;<sup id="cite_ref-140" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-140">&#91;135&#93;</a></sup> after a <a href="/wiki/1991_Soviet_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat_attempt" title="1991 Soviet coup d&#39;état attempt">putsch</a> of some Communist leaders in Moscow failed to depose Gorbachov, outright independence was <a href="/wiki/Declaration_of_Independence_of_Ukraine" title="Declaration of Independence of Ukraine">proclaimed</a> on 24 August 1991<sup id="cite_ref-141" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-141">&#91;136&#93;</a></sup> and approved by 92% of the Ukrainian electorate in a <a href="/wiki/1991_Ukrainian_independence_referendum" title="1991 Ukrainian independence referendum">referendum</a> on 1 December.<sup id="cite_ref-Nohlen_Stöver_142-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Nohlen_Stöver-142">&#91;137&#93;</a></sup> Ukraine's new <a href="/wiki/President_of_Ukraine" title="President of Ukraine">President</a>, Leonid Kravchuk, went on to sign the <a href="/wiki/Belavezha_Accords" class="mw-redirect" title="Belavezha Accords">Belavezha Accords</a> and made Ukraine a founding member of the much looser <a href="/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Independent_States" title="Commonwealth of Independent States">Commonwealth of Independent States</a> (CIS),<sup id="cite_ref-143" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-143">&#91;138&#93;</a></sup> though Ukraine never became a full member of the latter as it did not ratify the agreement founding CIS.<sup id="cite_ref-:2_144-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-144">&#91;139&#93;</a></sup> These documents sealed the fate of the Soviet Union, which formally voted itself out of existence on 26 December.<sup id="cite_ref-145" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-145">&#91;140&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Ukraine was initially viewed as having favourable economic conditions in comparison to the other regions of the Soviet Union,<sup id="cite_ref-146" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-146">&#91;141&#93;</a></sup> though it was one of the poorer Soviet republics by the end of the Soviet Union.<sup id="cite_ref-Notstronk_147-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Notstronk-147">&#91;142&#93;</a></sup> However, during its transition to the market economy, the country experienced deeper economic slowdown than almost all of the other <a href="/wiki/Former_Soviet_Republics" class="mw-redirect" title="Former Soviet Republics">former Soviet Republics</a>. During the recession, between 1991 and 1999, Ukraine lost 60% of its GDP<sup id="cite_ref-IMF_148-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-IMF-148">&#91;143&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-149" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-149">&#91;144&#93;</a></sup> and suffered from <a href="/wiki/Hyperinflation" title="Hyperinflation">hyperinflation</a> that peaked at 10,000% in 1993.<sup id="cite_ref-150" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-150">&#91;145&#93;</a></sup> The situation only stabilized well after the new currency, the <a href="/wiki/Hryvnia" class="mw-redirect" title="Hryvnia">hryvnia</a>, fell sharply in late 1998 partially as a fallout from the <a href="/wiki/Russian_debt_default" class="mw-redirect" title="Russian debt default">Russian debt default</a> earlier that year.<sup id="cite_ref-151" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-151">&#91;146&#93;</a></sup> The legacy of the economic policies of the nineties was the mass privatization of state property that created a class of extremely powerful and rich individuals known as the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_oligarch" class="mw-redirect" title="Ukrainian oligarch">oligarchs</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Notstronk_147-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Notstronk-147">&#91;142&#93;</a></sup> The country would then fall into sharp recessions as a result of the <a href="/wiki/2008_global_financial_crisis" class="mw-redirect" title="2008 global financial crisis">2008 global financial crisis</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Notstronk_147-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Notstronk-147">&#91;142&#93;</a></sup> then the start of the <a href="/wiki/Russo-Ukrainian_War" title="Russo-Ukrainian War">Russo-Ukrainian War</a> in 2014,<sup id="cite_ref-152" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-152">&#91;147&#93;</a></sup> and finally, the <a href="/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" class="mw-redirect" title="2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine">full-scale invasion</a> of Russia in starting from 24 February 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-153" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-153">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup> Ukraine's economy in general underperformed since the time independence came due to pervasive <a href="/wiki/Corruption_in_Ukraine" title="Corruption in Ukraine">corruption</a> and mismanagement,<sup id="cite_ref-154" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-154">&#91;149&#93;</a></sup> which, particularly in the 1990s, led to protests and organized strikes.<sup id="cite_ref-155" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-155">&#91;150&#93;</a></sup> The war with Russia impeded meaningful economic recovery in the 2010s,<sup id="cite_ref-156" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-156">&#91;151&#93;</a></sup> while efforts to combat the <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Ukraine" title="COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine">COVID-19 pandemic</a>, which arrived in 2020, were made much harder by <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_vaccine" title="COVID-19 vaccine">low vaccination rates</a><sup id="cite_ref-157" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-157">&#91;152&#93;</a></sup> and, later in the pandemic, by the ongoing invasion.<sup id="cite_ref-158" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-158">&#91;153&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Euromaidan_Kyiv_1-12-13_by_Gnatoush_009.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Euromaidan_Kyiv_1-12-13_by_Gnatoush_009.jpg/220px-Euromaidan_Kyiv_1-12-13_by_Gnatoush_009.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Euromaidan_Kyiv_1-12-13_by_Gnatoush_009.jpg/330px-Euromaidan_Kyiv_1-12-13_by_Gnatoush_009.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Euromaidan_Kyiv_1-12-13_by_Gnatoush_009.jpg/440px-Euromaidan_Kyiv_1-12-13_by_Gnatoush_009.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1200" data-file-height="800" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Euromaidan" title="Euromaidan">Euromaidan</a> protest in Kyiv, December 2013</figcaption></figure>
<p>From the political perspective, one of the defining features of the <a href="/wiki/Politics_of_Ukraine" title="Politics of Ukraine">politics of Ukraine</a> is that for most of the time, it has been divided along two issues: the relation between Ukraine, the <a href="/wiki/Western_world" title="Western world">West</a> and Russia, and the classical <a href="/wiki/Left%E2%80%93right_political_spectrum" title="Left–right political spectrum">left-right</a> divide.<sup id="cite_ref-159" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-159">&#91;154&#93;</a></sup> The first two presidents, Kravchuk and <a href="/wiki/Leonid_Kuchma" title="Leonid Kuchma">Leonid Kuchma</a>, tended to balance the competing visions of Ukraine,<sup id="cite_ref-160" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-160">&#91;155&#93;</a></sup> though <a href="/wiki/Yushchenko" class="mw-redirect" title="Yushchenko">Yushchenko</a> and <a href="/wiki/Yanukovych" class="mw-redirect" title="Yanukovych">Yanukovych</a> were generally pro-Western and pro-Russian, respectively. There were two major protests against Yanukovych: the <a href="/wiki/Orange_Revolution" title="Orange Revolution">Orange Revolution</a> in 2004, when tens of thousands of people went in protest of <a href="/wiki/Election_rigging" class="mw-redirect" title="Election rigging">election rigging</a> in his favour (Yushchenko was eventually elected president), and another one in the winter of 2013/2014, when more gathered on the <a href="/wiki/Euromaidan" title="Euromaidan">Euromaidan</a> to oppose Yanukovych's refusal to sign the <a href="/wiki/European_Union%E2%80%93Ukraine_Association_Agreement" title="European Union–Ukraine Association Agreement">European Union–Ukraine Association Agreement</a>. By the end of the 2014 protests, he fled from Ukraine and was removed by the parliament in what is termed the <a href="/wiki/Revolution_of_Dignity" title="Revolution of Dignity">Revolution of Dignity</a>, but Russia refused to recognize the interim pro-Western government, calling it a <i><a href="/wiki/Military_junta" title="Military junta">junta</a></i> and denouncing the events as a <a href="/wiki/Coup_d%27%C3%A9tat" title="Coup d&#39;état">coup d'état</a> sponsored by the United States.<sup id="cite_ref-161" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-161">&#91;156&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-162" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-162">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Partido_da_imprensa_Golpista_163-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Partido_da_imprensa_Golpista-163">&#91;158&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Even though Russia had signed the so-called <a href="/wiki/Budapest_Memorandum_on_Security_Assurances" class="mw-redirect" title="Budapest Memorandum on Security Assurances">Budapest memorandum</a> in 1994 that said that Ukraine was to hand over <a href="/wiki/Ukraine_and_weapons_of_mass_destruction" title="Ukraine and weapons of mass destruction">nuclear weapons</a> in exchange of security guarantees and those of territorial integrity, it reacted violently to these developments and started a <a href="/wiki/Russo-Ukrainian_War" title="Russo-Ukrainian War">war against its western neighbour</a>. In late February and early March 2014, it <a href="/wiki/Annexation_of_Crimea_by_the_Russian_Federation" title="Annexation of Crimea by the Russian Federation">annexed Crimea</a> using its <a href="/wiki/Russian_Navy" title="Russian Navy">Navy</a> in <a href="/wiki/Sevastopol_Naval_Base" title="Sevastopol Naval Base">Sevastopol</a> as well as the so-called <a href="/wiki/Little_green_men_(Russo-Ukrainian_War)" title="Little green men (Russo-Ukrainian War)">little green men</a>; after this succeeded, it then launched a <a href="/wiki/War_in_Donbas_(2014%E2%80%932022)" title="War in Donbas (2014–2022)">proxy war in the Donbas</a> via the breakaway <a href="/wiki/Donetsk_People%27s_Republic" title="Donetsk People&#39;s Republic">Donetsk People's Republic</a> and <a href="/wiki/Luhansk_People%27s_Republic" title="Luhansk People&#39;s Republic">Luhansk People's Republic</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-164" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-164">&#91;159&#93;</a></sup> The first months of the conflict with the Russian-backed separatists were fluid, but Russian forces then started an open invasion in Donbas on 24 August 2014. Together they pushed back Ukrainian troops to the frontline established in February 2015, i.e. after Ukrainian troops <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Debaltseve" title="Battle of Debaltseve">withdrew from Debaltseve</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-165" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-165">&#91;160&#93;</a></sup> The conflict remained in a sort of <a href="/wiki/Frozen_conflict" title="Frozen conflict">frozen state</a> until the early hours of 24 February 2022,<sup id="cite_ref-166" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-166">&#91;161&#93;</a></sup> when Russia proceeded with an <a href="/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" class="mw-redirect" title="2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine">ongoing invasion</a> of Ukraine.<sup id="cite_ref-167" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-167">&#91;162&#93;</a></sup> Russian troops control about 17% of Ukraine's internationally recognized territory, which constitutes 94% of <a href="/wiki/Luhansk_Oblast" title="Luhansk Oblast">Luhansk Oblast</a>, 73% of <a href="/wiki/Kherson_Oblast" title="Kherson Oblast">Kherson Oblast</a>, 72% of <a href="/wiki/Zaporizhzhia_Oblast" title="Zaporizhzhia Oblast">Zaporizhzhia Oblast</a>, 54% of <a href="/wiki/Donetsk_Oblast" title="Donetsk Oblast">Donetsk Oblast</a> and Crimea.<sup id="cite_ref-168" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-168">&#91;163&#93;</a></sup> though Russia failed with its initial plan, with Ukrainian troops recapturing some territory in counteroffensives.<sup id="cite_ref-169" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-169">&#91;164&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine.svg/220px-2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine.svg.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="148" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine.svg/330px-2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine.svg/440px-2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="2199" data-file-height="1478" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Russian-occupied_territories_of_Ukraine" title="Russian-occupied territories of Ukraine">Russian-occupied territories of Ukraine</a> as of 4 September 2023</figcaption></figure>
<p>The military conflict with Russia shifted the government's policy towards the West. Shortly after Yanukovych fled Ukraine, the country signed the EU association agreement in June 2014, and its citizens were granted visa-free travel to the European Union three years later. In January 2019, the <a href="/wiki/Orthodox_Church_of_Ukraine" title="Orthodox Church of Ukraine">Orthodox Church of Ukraine</a> was recognized as independent of Moscow, which reversed the <a href="/wiki/Annexation_of_the_Metropolitanate_of_Kyiv_by_the_Moscow_Patriarchate" title="Annexation of the Metropolitanate of Kyiv by the Moscow Patriarchate">1686 decision</a> of the patriarch of Constantinople and dealt a further blow to Moscow's influence in Ukraine.<sup id="cite_ref-170" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-170">&#91;165&#93;</a></sup> Finally, amid a full-scale war with Russia, Ukraine was granted <a href="/wiki/Potential_enlargement_of_the_European_Union" title="Potential enlargement of the European Union">candidate status</a> to the European Union on 23 June 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-BBC_News_171-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BBC_News-171">&#91;166&#93;</a></sup> A broad anti-corruption drive began in early 2023 with the resignations of several deputy ministers and regional heads during a reshuffle of the government.<sup id="cite_ref-172" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-172">&#91;167&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Geography">Geography</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Geography_of_Ukraine" title="Geography of Ukraine">Geography of Ukraine</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Topographic_map_of_Ukraine_(with_borders_and_towns).svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/Topographic_map_of_Ukraine_%28with_borders_and_towns%29.svg/220px-Topographic_map_of_Ukraine_%28with_borders_and_towns%29.svg.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/Topographic_map_of_Ukraine_%28with_borders_and_towns%29.svg/330px-Topographic_map_of_Ukraine_%28with_borders_and_towns%29.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/Topographic_map_of_Ukraine_%28with_borders_and_towns%29.svg/440px-Topographic_map_of_Ukraine_%28with_borders_and_towns%29.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1449" data-file-height="959" /></a><figcaption>Topographic map of Ukraine, with borders, cities and towns (territories of Ukraine <a href="/wiki/Russian-occupied_territories_of_Ukraine" title="Russian-occupied territories of Ukraine">occupied by Russia</a> before February 2022 are striped)</figcaption></figure>
<p>Ukraine is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_European_countries_by_area" title="List of European countries by area">second-largest European country</a>, after Russia. Lying between latitudes <a href="/wiki/44th_parallel_north" title="44th parallel north">44°</a> and <a href="/wiki/53rd_parallel_north" title="53rd parallel north">53° N</a>, and longitudes <a href="/wiki/22nd_meridian_east" title="22nd meridian east">22°</a> and <a href="/wiki/41st_meridian_east" title="41st meridian east">41° E</a>., it is mostly in the <a href="/wiki/East_European_Plain" title="East European Plain">East European Plain</a>. Ukraine covers an area of 603,550 square kilometres (233,030&#160;sq&#160;mi), with a coastline of 2,782 kilometres (1,729&#160;mi).<sup id="cite_ref-cia_52-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-52">&#91;49&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The landscape of Ukraine consists mostly of fertile <a href="/wiki/Steppes" class="mw-redirect" title="Steppes">steppes</a> (plains with few trees) and plateaus, crossed by rivers such as the <a href="/wiki/Dnieper_River" class="mw-redirect" title="Dnieper River">Dnieper</a> (<span title="Ukrainian-language text"><i lang="uk-Latn">Dnipro</i></span>), <a href="/wiki/Seversky_Donets" class="mw-redirect" title="Seversky Donets">Seversky Donets</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dniester" title="Dniester">Dniester</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Southern_Bug" title="Southern Bug">Southern Bug</a> as they flow south into the <a href="/wiki/Black_Sea" title="Black Sea">Black Sea</a> and the smaller <a href="/wiki/Sea_of_Azov" title="Sea of Azov">Sea of Azov</a>. To the southwest, the <a href="/wiki/Danube_Delta" title="Danube Delta">delta</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Danube" title="Danube">Danube</a> forms the border with Romania. Ukraine's various regions have diverse geographic features ranging from the highlands to the lowlands. The country's only mountains are the <a href="/wiki/Carpathian_Mountains" title="Carpathian Mountains">Carpathian Mountains</a> in the west, of which the highest is <a href="/wiki/Hoverla" title="Hoverla">Hoverla</a> at 2,061 metres (6,762&#160;ft), and the <a href="/wiki/Crimean_Mountains" title="Crimean Mountains">Crimean Mountains</a>, in the extreme south along the coast.<sup id="cite_ref-173" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-173">&#91;168&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Ukraine also has a number of highland regions such as the <a href="/wiki/Volhynian-Podolian_Upland" title="Volhynian-Podolian Upland">Volyn-Podillia Upland</a> (in the west) and the Near-Dnipro Upland (on the right bank of the Dnieper). To the east there are the south-western spurs of the <a href="/wiki/Central_Russian_Upland" title="Central Russian Upland">Central Russian Upland</a> over which runs the border with Russia. Near the <a href="/wiki/Sea_of_Azov" title="Sea of Azov">Sea of Azov</a> are the Donets Ridge and the Near Azov Upland. The <a href="/wiki/Snow_melt" class="mw-redirect" title="Snow melt">snow melt</a> from the mountains feeds the rivers and their <a href="/wiki/Waterfalls_of_Ukraine" class="mw-redirect" title="Waterfalls of Ukraine">waterfalls</a>.
</p><p>Significant natural resources in Ukraine include <a href="/wiki/Lithium" title="Lithium">lithium</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-174" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-174">&#91;169&#93;</a></sup> natural gas,<sup id="cite_ref-:0_175-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-175">&#91;170&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Kaolin" class="mw-redirect" title="Kaolin">kaolin</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-:0_175-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-175">&#91;170&#93;</a></sup> timber<sup id="cite_ref-176" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-176">&#91;171&#93;</a></sup> and an abundance of <a href="/wiki/Arable_land" title="Arable land">arable land</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-177" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-177">&#91;172&#93;</a></sup> Ukraine has many environmental issues.<sup id="cite_ref-178" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-178">&#91;173&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-179" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-179">&#91;174&#93;</a></sup> Some regions lack adequate supplies of potable water.<sup id="cite_ref-180" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-180">&#91;175&#93;</a></sup> Air and water pollution affects the country, as well as deforestation, and radiation contamination in the northeast from the 1986 accident at the <a href="/wiki/Chernobyl" title="Chernobyl">Chernobyl</a> Nuclear Power Plant.<sup id="cite_ref-181" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-181">&#91;176&#93;</a></sup> The environmental damage caused by the <a href="/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" title="Russian invasion of Ukraine">Russian invasion of Ukraine</a> has been described as an <a href="/wiki/Ecocide" title="Ecocide">ecocide</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Destruction_of_the_Kakhovka_Dam" title="Destruction of the Kakhovka Dam">destruction</a> of <a href="/wiki/Kakhovka_Dam" title="Kakhovka Dam">Kakhovka Dam</a>, severe pollution and millions of tonnes of contaminated debris is estimated to cost <a href="/wiki/USD" class="mw-redirect" title="USD">USD</a> 51 billion to repair.<sup id="cite_ref-pax_182-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-pax-182">&#91;177&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-enviroyale_183-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-enviroyale-183">&#91;178&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-184" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-184">&#91;179&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-185" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-185">&#91;180&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-186" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-186">&#91;181&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-187" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-187">&#91;182&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-188" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-188">&#91;183&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Climate">Climate</span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Koppen-Geiger_Map_UKR_present.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/Koppen-Geiger_Map_UKR_present.svg/260px-Koppen-Geiger_Map_UKR_present.svg.png" decoding="async" width="260" height="122" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/Koppen-Geiger_Map_UKR_present.svg/390px-Koppen-Geiger_Map_UKR_present.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/Koppen-Geiger_Map_UKR_present.svg/520px-Koppen-Geiger_Map_UKR_present.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1816" data-file-height="850" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification" title="Köppen climate classification">Köppen climate classification</a> map of Ukraine</figcaption></figure>
<p>Ukraine has a mostly <a href="/wiki/Temperate_climate" title="Temperate climate">temperate climate</a>, except for the southern coast of Crimea which has a <a href="/wiki/Subtropical_climate" class="mw-redirect" title="Subtropical climate">subtropical climate</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-faoclimate_189-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-faoclimate-189">&#91;184&#93;</a></sup> The climate is influenced by moderately warm, humid air from the Atlantic Ocean.<sup id="cite_ref-ebclimate_190-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ebclimate-190">&#91;185&#93;</a></sup> Average annual temperatures range from 5.5–7&#160;°C (41.9–44.6&#160;°F) in the north, to 11–13&#160;°C (51.8–55.4&#160;°F) in the south.<sup id="cite_ref-ebclimate_190-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ebclimate-190">&#91;185&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Precipitation_(meteorology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Precipitation (meteorology)">Precipitation</a> is highest in the west and north and lowest in the east and southeast.<sup id="cite_ref-ebclimate_190-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ebclimate-190">&#91;185&#93;</a></sup> Western Ukraine, particularly in the Carpathian Mountains, receives around 120 centimetres (47.2&#160;in) of precipitation annually, while Crimea and the coastal areas of the Black Sea receive around 40 centimetres (15.7&#160;in).<sup id="cite_ref-ebclimate_190-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ebclimate-190">&#91;185&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Water availability from the major river basins is expected to decrease <a href="/wiki/Effects_of_climate_change" title="Effects of climate change">due to climate change</a>, especially in summer. This poses risks to the agricultural sector.<sup id="cite_ref-191" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-191">&#91;186&#93;</a></sup> The negative <a href="/wiki/Effects_of_climate_change_on_agriculture" title="Effects of climate change on agriculture">impacts of climate change on agriculture</a> are mostly felt in the south of the country, which has a <a href="/wiki/Steppe" title="Steppe">steppe</a> climate. In the north, some crops may be able to benefit from a longer growing season.<sup id="cite_ref-192" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-192">&#91;187&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/World_Bank" title="World Bank">World Bank</a> has stated that Ukraine is highly <a href="/wiki/Climate_change_vulnerability" title="Climate change vulnerability">vulnerable to climate change</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-193" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-193">&#91;188&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Biodiversity">Biodiversity</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Wildlife_of_Ukraine" title="Wildlife of Ukraine">Wildlife of Ukraine</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:WLE_-_2020_-_%D0%90%D0%B9-%D0%9F%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%80%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%81%D1%8C%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D1%8F%D0%B9%D0%BB%D0%B0.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/WLE_-_2020_-_%D0%90%D0%B9-%D0%9F%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%80%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%81%D1%8C%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D1%8F%D0%B9%D0%BB%D0%B0.jpg/220px-WLE_-_2020_-_%D0%90%D0%B9-%D0%9F%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%80%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%81%D1%8C%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D1%8F%D0%B9%D0%BB%D0%B0.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/WLE_-_2020_-_%D0%90%D0%B9-%D0%9F%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%80%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%81%D1%8C%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D1%8F%D0%B9%D0%BB%D0%B0.jpg/330px-WLE_-_2020_-_%D0%90%D0%B9-%D0%9F%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%80%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%81%D1%8C%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D1%8F%D0%B9%D0%BB%D0%B0.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/WLE_-_2020_-_%D0%90%D0%B9-%D0%9F%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%80%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%81%D1%8C%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D1%8F%D0%B9%D0%BB%D0%B0.jpg/440px-WLE_-_2020_-_%D0%90%D0%B9-%D0%9F%D0%B5%D1%82%D1%80%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%81%D1%8C%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D1%8F%D0%B9%D0%BB%D0%B0.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4446" data-file-height="2963" /></a><figcaption>View from the western slope of Mount Ai-Petri of the <a href="/wiki/Ai-Petri" title="Ai-Petri">Ai-Petri</a> plateau, in Crimea designated by the Ukrainian government as a natural heritage site.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Ukraine contains six terrestrial <a href="/wiki/Ecoregion" title="Ecoregion">ecoregions</a>: <a href="/wiki/Central_European_mixed_forests" title="Central European mixed forests">Central European mixed forests</a>, <a href="/wiki/Crimean_Submediterranean_forest_complex" title="Crimean Submediterranean forest complex">Crimean Submediterranean forest complex</a>, <a href="/wiki/East_European_forest_steppe" title="East European forest steppe">East European forest steppe</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pannonian_mixed_forests" title="Pannonian mixed forests">Pannonian mixed forests</a>, <a href="/wiki/Carpathian_montane_conifer_forests" title="Carpathian montane conifer forests">Carpathian montane conifer forests</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Pontic_steppe" class="mw-redirect" title="Pontic steppe">Pontic steppe</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-DinersteinOlson2017_194-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-DinersteinOlson2017-194">&#91;189&#93;</a></sup> There is somewhat more <a href="/wiki/Conifer" title="Conifer">coniferous</a> than <a href="/wiki/Deciduous" title="Deciduous">deciduous</a> forest.<sup id="cite_ref-ShvidenkoBukshaKrakovska2017_195-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ShvidenkoBukshaKrakovska2017-195">&#91;190&#93;</a></sup> The most densely forested area is <a href="/wiki/Polisia" class="mw-redirect" title="Polisia">Polisia</a> in the northwest, with pine, oak, and birch.<sup id="cite_ref-ShvidenkoBukshaKrakovska2017_195-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ShvidenkoBukshaKrakovska2017-195">&#91;190&#93;</a></sup> There are 45,000 species of animals (mostly invertebrates),<sup id="cite_ref-Conference2001_196-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Conference2001-196">&#91;191&#93;</a></sup> with approximately 385 endangered species listed in the <a href="/wiki/Red_Data_Book_of_Ukraine" title="Red Data Book of Ukraine">Red Data Book of Ukraine</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-State_197-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-State-197">&#91;192&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Ramsar_site" title="Ramsar site">Internationally important wetlands</a> cover over 7,000 square kilometres (2,700&#160;sq&#160;mi), with the <a href="/wiki/Danube_Delta" title="Danube Delta">Danube Delta</a> being important for conservation.<sup id="cite_ref-wetland_198-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-wetland-198">&#91;193&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Ramsar_199-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ramsar-199">&#91;194&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Urban_areas">Urban areas</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Ukraine" title="List of cities in Ukraine">List of cities in Ukraine</a></div>
<p>Ukraine has 457 cities, of which 176 are designated as oblast-class, 279 as smaller <span title="Ukrainian-language text"><i lang="uk-Latn">raion</i></span>-class cities, and two as special legal status cities. There are also 886 urban-type settlements and 28,552 villages.<sup id="cite_ref-oblasts_200-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-oblasts-200">&#91;195&#93;</a></sup>
</p>

<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Politics">Politics</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Politics_of_Ukraine" title="Politics of Ukraine">Politics of Ukraine</a></div>
<p>Ukraine is a republic under a <a href="/wiki/Semi-presidential_system" class="mw-redirect" title="Semi-presidential system">semi-presidential system</a> with separate <a href="/wiki/Legislative_branch" class="mw-redirect" title="Legislative branch">legislative</a>, <a href="/wiki/Executive_branch" class="mw-redirect" title="Executive branch">executive</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Judicial_branch" class="mw-redirect" title="Judicial branch">judicial branches</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Choudhry_2018_p16._202-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Choudhry_2018_p16.-202">&#91;197&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Constitution">Constitution</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Ukraine" title="Constitution of Ukraine">Constitution of Ukraine</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Chart_Constitution_of_Ukraine_EN.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/Chart_Constitution_of_Ukraine_EN.svg/260px-Chart_Constitution_of_Ukraine_EN.svg.png" decoding="async" width="260" height="184" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/Chart_Constitution_of_Ukraine_EN.svg/390px-Chart_Constitution_of_Ukraine_EN.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/Chart_Constitution_of_Ukraine_EN.svg/520px-Chart_Constitution_of_Ukraine_EN.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1052" data-file-height="744" /></a><figcaption>Chart of the political system of Ukraine</figcaption></figure>
<p>The Constitution of Ukraine was adopted and ratified at the 5th session of the <a href="/wiki/Verkhovna_Rada" title="Verkhovna Rada">Verkhovna Rada</a>, the parliament of Ukraine, on 28 June 1996.<sup id="cite_ref-UNIANCD28616_203-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UNIANCD28616-203">&#91;198&#93;</a></sup> The constitution was passed with 315 ayes out of 450 votes possible (300 ayes minimum).<sup id="cite_ref-UNIANCD28616_203-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UNIANCD28616-203">&#91;198&#93;</a></sup> All other laws and other normative<sup class="noprint Inline-Template" style="margin-left:0.1em; white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Please_clarify" title="Wikipedia:Please clarify"><span title="The text near this tag may need clarification or removal of jargon. (March 2022)">clarification needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> legal acts of Ukraine must conform to the constitution. The right to amend the constitution through a special legislative procedure is vested exclusively in the parliament. The only body that may interpret the constitution and determine whether legislation conforms to it is the <a href="/wiki/Constitutional_Court_of_Ukraine" title="Constitutional Court of Ukraine">Constitutional Court of Ukraine</a>. Since 1996, the <a href="/wiki/Public_holiday" title="Public holiday">public holiday</a> <a href="/wiki/Constitution_Day_(Ukraine)" title="Constitution Day (Ukraine)">Constitution Day</a> is celebrated on 28 June.<sup id="cite_ref-204" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-204">&#91;199&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-UW29121996_205-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UW29121996-205">&#91;200&#93;</a></sup> On 7 February 2019, the Verkhovna Rada voted to amend the constitution to state Ukraine's strategic objectives as joining the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a> and <a href="/wiki/NATO" title="NATO">NATO</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-206" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-206">&#91;201&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Government">Government</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Government_of_Ukraine" title="Government of Ukraine">Government of Ukraine</a></div>
