</p>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:cyan; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Ukrainians" title="Ukrainians">Ukrainians</a> (77.8%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:blue; color:white;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Russians" title="Russians">Russians</a> (17.3%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:yellow; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Romanians_in_Ukraine" title="Romanians in Ukraine">Romanians</a> and <a href="/wiki/Moldovans_in_Ukraine" title="Moldovans in Ukraine">Moldovans</a> (0.8%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:red; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Belarusians_in_Ukraine" title="Belarusians in Ukraine">Belarusians</a> (0.6%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:brown; color:white;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Crimean_Tatars" title="Crimean Tatars">Crimean&#160;Tatars</a> (0.5%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:green; color:white;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Bulgarians_in_Ukraine" title="Bulgarians in Ukraine">Bulgarians</a> (0.4%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:pink; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Hungarians_in_Ukraine" title="Hungarians in Ukraine">Hungarians</a> (0.3%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:purple; color:white;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Poles_in_Ukraine" title="Poles in Ukraine">Poles</a> (0.3%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:black; color:white;">&#160;</span>&#160;other (2%)</div>
</div>
</div></div>
<p>Before the <a href="/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" class="mw-redirect" title="2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine">2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine</a> the country had an estimated population of over 41 million people, and was the <a href="/wiki/List_of_European_countries_by_population" title="List of European countries by population">eighth-most populous country</a> in Europe. It is a <a href="/wiki/Urbanization_by_country" class="mw-redirect" title="Urbanization by country">heavily urbanized country</a>, and its industrial regions in the east and southeast are the most densely populated—about 67% of its total population lives in urban areas.<sup id="cite_ref-291" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-291">&#91;286&#93;</a></sup> At that time Ukraine had a <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_population_density" class="mw-redirect" title="List of countries by population density">population density</a> of 69.5 inhabitants&#160;per square kilometre (180 inhabitants/sq&#160;mi), and the overall <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy" title="List of countries by life expectancy">life expectancy in the country</a> at birth was 73 years (68 years for males and 77.8 years for females).<sup id="cite_ref-292" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-292">&#91;287&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Following the <a href="/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union" title="Dissolution of the Soviet Union">dissolution of the Soviet Union</a>, Ukraine's population hit a peak of roughly 52 million in 1993. However, due to its <a href="/wiki/Death_rate" class="mw-redirect" title="Death rate">death rate</a> exceeding its <a href="/wiki/Birth_rate" title="Birth rate">birth rate</a>, mass emigration, poor living conditions, and low-quality health care,<sup id="cite_ref-nw-20260217_293-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nw-20260217-293">&#91;288&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-ukrstat-population_294-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ukrstat-population-294">&#91;289&#93;</a></sup> the total population decreased by 6.6 million, or 12.8% from the same year to 2014.
</p><p>According to the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Census_(2001)" class="mw-redirect" title="Ukrainian Census (2001)">2001 census</a>, ethnic <a href="/wiki/Ukrainians" title="Ukrainians">Ukrainians</a> made up roughly 78% of the population, while <a href="/wiki/Russians_in_Ukraine" title="Russians in Ukraine">Russians</a> were the largest minority, at some 17.3% of the population. Small minority populations included: <a href="/wiki/Belarusians" title="Belarusians">Belarusians</a> (0.6%), <a href="/wiki/Moldovans" title="Moldovans">Moldovans</a> (0.5%), <a href="/wiki/Crimean_Tatars" title="Crimean Tatars">Crimean Tatars</a> (0.5%), <a href="/wiki/Bulgarians" title="Bulgarians">Bulgarians</a> (0.4%), <a href="/wiki/Hungarians" title="Hungarians">Hungarians</a> (0.3%), <a href="/wiki/Romanians" title="Romanians">Romanians</a> (0.3%), <a href="/wiki/Polish_people" title="Polish people">Poles</a> (0.3%), <a href="/wiki/Jews" title="Jews">Jews</a> (0.3%), <a href="/wiki/Armenians" title="Armenians">Armenians</a> (0.2%), <a href="/wiki/Greeks" title="Greeks">Greeks</a> (0.2%) and <a href="/wiki/Tatars" title="Tatars">Tatars</a> (0.2%).<sup id="cite_ref-Ethnic_composition_of_the_population_of_Ukraine,_2001_Census_2-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ethnic_composition_of_the_population_of_Ukraine,_2001_Census-2">&#91;2&#93;</a></sup> It was also estimated that there were about 10–40,000 <a href="/wiki/Koreans" title="Koreans">Koreans</a> in Ukraine, who lived mostly in the south of the country, belonging to the historical <a href="/wiki/Koryo-saram" title="Koryo-saram">Koryo-saram</a> group.<sup id="cite_ref-295" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-295">&#91;290&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-296" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-296">&#91;291&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Outside the former Soviet Union, the largest source of incoming immigrants in Ukraine's post-independence period was from four Asian countries, namely China, India, Pakistan and Afghanistan.<sup id="cite_ref-mp_297-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mp-297">&#91;292&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In the late 2010s 1.4 million Ukrainians were <a href="/wiki/Internally_displaced" class="mw-redirect" title="Internally displaced">internally displaced</a> due to the <a href="/wiki/War_in_Donbas_(2014%E2%80%932022)" title="War in Donbas (2014–2022)">war in Donbas</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-298" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-298">&#91;293&#93;</a></sup> and in early 2022 over 4.1 million fled the country in the aftermath of the <a href="/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" class="mw-redirect" title="2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine">Russian invasion</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-299" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-299">&#91;294&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Language">Language</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Languages_of_Ukraine" title="Languages of Ukraine">Languages of Ukraine</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_language" title="Ukrainian language">Ukrainian language</a> and <a href="/wiki/Russian_language_in_Ukraine" title="Russian language in Ukraine">Russian language in Ukraine</a></div>
<p>According to Ukraine's constitution, the <a href="/wiki/Official_language" title="Official language">state language</a> is <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_language" title="Ukrainian language">Ukrainian</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-SerhyYUBoaMN_300-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-SerhyYUBoaMN-300">&#91;295&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Russian_language" title="Russian language">Russian</a> is widely spoken in the country, especially in eastern and southern Ukraine.<sup id="cite_ref-SerhyYUBoaMN_300-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-SerhyYUBoaMN-300">&#91;295&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-301" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-301">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup> Most native Ukrainian speakers know Russian as a second language.<sup id="cite_ref-SerhyYUBoaMN_300-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-SerhyYUBoaMN-300">&#91;295&#93;</a></sup> Russian was the <i>de facto</i> dominant language of the Soviet Union but Ukrainian also held official status in the republic,<sup id="cite_ref-302" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-302">&#91;297&#93;</a></sup> and in the schools of the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_SSR" class="mw-redirect" title="Ukrainian SSR">Ukrainian SSR</a>, learning Ukrainian was mandatory.<sup id="cite_ref-SerhyYUBoaMN_300-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-SerhyYUBoaMN-300">&#91;295&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:UkraineNativeLanguagesCensus2001detailed-en.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/UkraineNativeLanguagesCensus2001detailed-en.png/290px-UkraineNativeLanguagesCensus2001detailed-en.png" decoding="async" width="290" height="200" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/UkraineNativeLanguagesCensus2001detailed-en.png/435px-UkraineNativeLanguagesCensus2001detailed-en.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/UkraineNativeLanguagesCensus2001detailed-en.png/580px-UkraineNativeLanguagesCensus2001detailed-en.png 2x" data-file-width="2500" data-file-height="1720" /></a><figcaption>Linguistic map of Ukraine showing most common native language by city, town, or village council, according to the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Census_(2001)" class="mw-redirect" title="Ukrainian Census (2001)">2001 census</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Effective in August 2012, <a href="/wiki/Legislation_on_languages_in_Ukraine" class="mw-redirect" title="Legislation on languages in Ukraine">a new law on regional languages</a> entitled any local language spoken by at least a 10&#160;percent minority be declared official within that area.<sup id="cite_ref-303" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-303">&#91;298&#93;</a></sup> Within weeks, Russian was declared a regional language of several southern and eastern <a href="/wiki/Oblasts_of_Ukraine" title="Oblasts of Ukraine">oblasts</a> (provinces) and cities.<sup id="cite_ref-304" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-304">&#91;299&#93;</a></sup> Russian could then be used in the administrative office work and documents of those places.<sup id="cite_ref-NewUklang2892012_305-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NewUklang2892012-305">&#91;300&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-306" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-306">&#91;301&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 23 February 2014, following the <a href="/wiki/Revolution_of_Dignity" title="Revolution of Dignity">Revolution of Dignity</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Parliament" class="mw-redirect" title="Ukrainian Parliament">Ukrainian Parliament</a> voted to repeal the law on regional languages, making Ukrainian the sole state language at all levels; however, the repeal was not signed by acting <a href="/wiki/Oleksandr_Turchynov" title="Oleksandr Turchynov">President Turchynov</a> or by President Poroshenko.<sup id="cite_ref-307" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-307">&#91;302&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-308" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-308">&#91;303&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-309" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-309">&#91;304&#93;</a></sup> In February 2019, the law allowing for official use of regional languages was found unconstitutional.<sup id="cite_ref-310" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-310">&#91;305&#93;</a></sup> According to the Council of Europe, this act fails to achieve fair protection of the <a href="/wiki/Linguistic_rights" title="Linguistic rights">linguistic rights</a> of <a href="/wiki/Minority_language" title="Minority language">minorities</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-311" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-311">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Ukrainian is the primary language used in the vast majority of Ukraine. 67% of Ukrainians speak Ukrainian as their primary language, while 30% speak Russian as their primary language.<sup id="cite_ref-312" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-312">&#91;307&#93;</a></sup> In eastern and southern Ukraine, Russian is the primary language in some cities, while Ukrainian is used in rural areas. <a href="/wiki/Hungarian_language" title="Hungarian language">Hungarian</a> is spoken in <a href="/wiki/Zakarpattia_Oblast" title="Zakarpattia Oblast">Zakarpattia Oblast</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-unian.info_313-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-unian.info-313">&#91;308&#93;</a></sup> There is no consensus among scholars whether <a href="/wiki/Rusyn_language" title="Rusyn language">Rusyn</a>, also spoken in Zakarpattia, is a distinct language or a dialect of Ukrainian.<sup id="cite_ref-314" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-314">&#91;309&#93;</a></sup> The Ukrainian government does not recognise Rusyn and <a href="/wiki/Rusyns" title="Rusyns">Rusyns</a> as a distinct language and people.<sup id="cite_ref-315" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-315">&#91;310&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>For a large part of the Soviet era, the number of Ukrainian speakers declined from generation to generation, and by the mid-1980s, the usage of the Ukrainian language in public life had decreased significantly.<sup id="cite_ref-Shamshur_316-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Shamshur-316">&#91;311&#93;</a></sup> Following independence, the government of Ukraine began restoring the use of the Ukrainian language in schools and government through a policy of <a href="/wiki/Ukrainisation" class="mw-redirect" title="Ukrainisation">Ukrainisation</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-317" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-317">&#91;312&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-318" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-318">&#91;313&#93;</a></sup> Today, most foreign films and TV programs, including Russian ones, are subtitled or dubbed in Ukrainian.<sup id="cite_ref-319" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-319">&#91;314&#93;</a></sup> Ukraine's 2017 <a href="/wiki/Education_in_Ukraine" title="Education in Ukraine">education law</a> bars primary education in public schools in grade five and up in any language but Ukrainian.<sup id="cite_ref-320" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-320">&#91;315&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-321" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-321">&#91;316&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Diaspora">Diaspora</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_diaspora" title="Ukrainian diaspora">Ukrainian diaspora</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Map_of_the_Ukrainian_Diaspora_in_the_World.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/Map_of_the_Ukrainian_Diaspora_in_the_World.svg/260px-Map_of_the_Ukrainian_Diaspora_in_the_World.svg.png" decoding="async" width="260" height="135" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/Map_of_the_Ukrainian_Diaspora_in_the_World.svg/390px-Map_of_the_Ukrainian_Diaspora_in_the_World.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/Map_of_the_Ukrainian_Diaspora_in_the_World.svg/520px-Map_of_the_Ukrainian_Diaspora_in_the_World.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="2192" data-file-height="1135" /></a><figcaption>A 2020 map of the Ukrainian diaspora in the world.<br /> <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#000000; color:white;">&#160;</span>&#160;Ukraine</div> <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#002c61ff; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;+ 1,000,000</div> <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#0057b7ff; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;+ 100,000</div> <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#66b0ffff; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;+ 10,000</div> <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#c7e2ffff; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;+ 1,000</div></figcaption></figure>
<p>The Ukrainian <a href="/wiki/Diaspora" title="Diaspora">diaspora</a> comprises <a href="/wiki/Ukrainians" title="Ukrainians">Ukrainians</a> and their descendants who live outside Ukraine around the world, especially those who maintain some kind of connection  to the land of their ancestors and maintain their feeling of Ukrainian national identity within their own local community.<sup id="cite_ref-322" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-322">&#91;317&#93;</a></sup> The Ukrainian diaspora is found throughout numerous regions worldwide including other <a href="/wiki/Post-Soviet_states" title="Post-Soviet states">post-Soviet states</a> as well as in <a href="/wiki/Canadian_Ukrainian" title="Canadian Ukrainian">Canada</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Cecco_2022_u131_323-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Cecco_2022_u131-323">&#91;318&#93;</a></sup> and other countries such as <a href="/wiki/Ukrainians_in_Poland" title="Ukrainians in Poland">Poland</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-324" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-324">&#91;319&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Americans" title="Ukrainian Americans">the United States</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-325" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-325">&#91;320&#93;</a></sup> the UK<sup id="cite_ref-326" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-326">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-327" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-327">&#91;322&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Brazil" title="Brazil">Brazil</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-328" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-328">&#91;323&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The  2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine has led to <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_refugee_crisis" class="mw-redirect" title="Ukrainian refugee crisis">millions of Ukrainian civilians moving</a> to neighbouring countries. Most crossed into Poland, Slovakia, and the Czech Republic, and others proceeded to at least temporarily settle in Hungary, Moldova, Germany, Austria, Romania and other European countries.<sup id="cite_ref-329" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-329">&#91;324&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Religion">Religion</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Religion_in_Ukraine" title="Religion in Ukraine">Religion in Ukraine</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:80-391-0151_Kyiv_St.Sophia%27s_Cathedral_RB_18_2_(cropped).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/80-391-0151_Kyiv_St.Sophia%27s_Cathedral_RB_18_2_%28cropped%29.jpg/220px-80-391-0151_Kyiv_St.Sophia%27s_Cathedral_RB_18_2_%28cropped%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/80-391-0151_Kyiv_St.Sophia%27s_Cathedral_RB_18_2_%28cropped%29.jpg/330px-80-391-0151_Kyiv_St.Sophia%27s_Cathedral_RB_18_2_%28cropped%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/80-391-0151_Kyiv_St.Sophia%27s_Cathedral_RB_18_2_%28cropped%29.jpg/440px-80-391-0151_Kyiv_St.Sophia%27s_Cathedral_RB_18_2_%28cropped%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4800" data-file-height="3603" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Saint_Sophia%27s_Cathedral,_Kyiv" class="mw-redirect" title="Saint Sophia&#39;s Cathedral, Kyiv">Saint Sophia Cathedral in Kyiv</a>, a <a href="/wiki/UNESCO" title="UNESCO">UNESCO</a> <a href="/wiki/World_Heritage_Site" title="World Heritage Site">World Heritage Site</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-330" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-330">&#91;325&#93;</a></sup> is one of the main Christian cathedrals in Ukraine.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Ukraine has the world's <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Orthodoxy_by_country" title="Eastern Orthodoxy by country">second-largest Eastern Orthodox population</a>, after Russia.<sup id="cite_ref-331" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-331">&#91;326&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-332" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-332">&#91;327&#93;</a></sup> A 2021 survey conducted by the <a href="/wiki/Kyiv_International_Institute_of_Sociology" title="Kyiv International Institute of Sociology">Kyiv International Institute of Sociology</a> (KIIS) found that 82% of Ukrainians declared themselves to be religious, while 7% were <a href="/wiki/Atheists" class="mw-redirect" title="Atheists">atheists</a>, and a further 11% found it difficult to answer the question.<sup id="cite_ref-333" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-333">&#91;328&#93;</a></sup> The level of religiosity in Ukraine was reported to be the highest in <a href="/wiki/Western_Ukraine" title="Western Ukraine">Western Ukraine</a> (91%), and the lowest in the <a href="/wiki/Donbas" title="Donbas">Donbas</a> (57%) and <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Ukraine" title="Eastern Ukraine">Eastern Ukraine</a> (56%).<sup id="cite_ref-Razumkov2016Page27_334-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Razumkov2016Page27-334">&#91;329&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2019, 82% of Ukrainians were Christians; out of which 72.7% declared themselves to be <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Church" title="Eastern Orthodox Church">Eastern Orthodox</a>, 8.8% <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Greek_Catholic_Church" title="Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church">Ukrainian Greek Catholics</a>, 2.3% <a href="/wiki/Protestantism" title="Protestantism">Protestants</a> and 0.9% <a href="/wiki/Latin_Church" title="Latin Church">Latin Church Catholics</a>. Other <a href="/wiki/Christian" class="mw-redirect" title="Christian">Christians</a> comprised 2.3%. <a href="/wiki/Judaism" title="Judaism">Judaism</a>, <a href="/wiki/Islam" title="Islam">Islam</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Hinduism" title="Hinduism">Hinduism</a> were the religions of 0.2% of the population each. According to the KIIS study, roughly 58.3% of the Ukrainian Orthodox population were members of the <a href="/wiki/Orthodox_Church_of_Ukraine" title="Orthodox Church of Ukraine">Orthodox Church of Ukraine</a>, and 25.4% were members of the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Orthodox_Church_(Moscow_Patriarchate)" title="Ukrainian Orthodox Church (Moscow Patriarchate)">Ukrainian Orthodox Church (Moscow Patriarchate)</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-335" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-335">&#91;330&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Protestants_in_Ukraine" class="mw-redirect" title="Protestants in Ukraine">Protestants</a> are a growing community in Ukraine, who made up 1.9% of the population in 2016,<sup id="cite_ref-Razumkov2016Page29_336-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Razumkov2016Page29-336">&#91;331&#93;</a></sup> but rose to 2.2% of the population in 2018.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Health">Health</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Health_in_Ukraine" <p>Ukraine's healthcare system is state subsidised and freely available to all Ukrainian citizens and registered residents. However, it is not compulsory to be treated in a state-run hospital as a number of private medical complexes do exist nationwide.<sup id="cite_ref-337" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-337">&#91;332&#93;</a></sup> The public sector employs most healthcare professionals, with those working for private medical centres typically also retaining their state employment as they are mandated to provide care at public health facilities on a regular basis.<sup id="cite_ref-338" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-338">&#91;333&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:%D0%9C%D1%96%D1%81%D1%8C%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D0%B4%D0%B8%D1%82%D1%8F%D1%87%D0%B0_%D0%BB%D1%96%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%80%D0%BD%D1%8F_(%D0%9A%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%87%D1%83%D0%BA)_-_04.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/af/%D0%9C%D1%96%D1%81%D1%8C%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D0%B4%D0%B8%D1%82%D1%8F%D1%87%D0%B0_%D0%BB%D1%96%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%80%D0%BD%D1%8F_%28%D0%9A%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%87%D1%83%D0%BA%29_-_04.JPG/200px-%D0%9C%D1%96%D1%81%D1%8C%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D0%B4%D0%B8%D1%82%D1%8F%D1%87%D0%B0_%D0%BB%D1%96%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%80%D0%BD%D1%8F_%28%D0%9A%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%87%D1%83%D0%BA%29_-_04.JPG" decoding="async" width="200" height="150" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/af/%D0%9C%D1%96%D1%81%D1%8C%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D0%B4%D0%B8%D1%82%D1%8F%D1%87%D0%B0_%D0%BB%D1%96%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%80%D0%BD%D1%8F_%28%D0%9A%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%87%D1%83%D0%BA%29_-_04.JPG/300px-%D0%9C%D1%96%D1%81%D1%8C%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D0%B4%D0%B8%D1%82%D1%8F%D1%87%D0%B0_%D0%BB%D1%96%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%80%D0%BD%D1%8F_%28%D0%9A%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%87%D1%83%D0%BA%29_-_04.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/af/%D0%9C%D1%96%D1%81%D1%8C%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D0%B4%D0%B8%D1%82%D1%8F%D1%87%D0%B0_%D0%BB%D1%96%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%80%D0%BD%D1%8F_%28%D0%9A%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%87%D1%83%D0%BA%29_-_04.JPG/400px-%D0%9C%D1%96%D1%81%D1%8C%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D0%B4%D0%B8%D1%82%D1%8F%D1%87%D0%B0_%D0%BB%D1%96%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%80%D0%BD%D1%8F_%28%D0%9A%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%87%D1%83%D0%BA%29_-_04.JPG 2x" data-file-width="4320" data-file-height="3240" /></a><figcaption>The municipal children's hospital in <a href="/wiki/Kremenchuk" title="Kremenchuk">Kremenchuk</a>, <a href="/wiki/Poltava_Oblast" title="Poltava Oblast">Poltava Oblast</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>All of Ukraine's medical service providers and hospitals are subordinate to the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Healthcare_(Ukraine)" class="mw-redirect" title="Ministry of Healthcare (Ukraine)">Ministry of Healthcare</a>, which provides oversight and scrutiny of general medical practice as well as being responsible for the day-to-day administration of the healthcare system. Despite this, standards of hygiene and patient-care have fallen.<sup id="cite_ref-339" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-339">&#91;334&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Ukraine faces a number of major public health issues and is considered to be in a demographic crisis because of its high death rate and low birth rate (the Ukrainian birth rate is 11 births/1,000 population, and the death rate is 16.3 deaths/1,000 population).<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (October 2022)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> A factor contributing to the high death rate is a high <a href="/wiki/Mortality_rate" title="Mortality rate">mortality rate</a> among working-age males from preventable causes such as <a href="/wiki/Alcohol_poisoning" class="mw-redirect" title="Alcohol poisoning">alcohol poisoning</a> and smoking.<sup id="cite_ref-worldbank1_340-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-worldbank1-340">&#91;335&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Active reformation of Ukraine's healthcare system was initiated right after the appointment of <a href="/wiki/Ulana_Suprun" title="Ulana Suprun">Ulana Suprun</a> as a head of the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Healthcare_(Ukraine)" class="mw-redirect" title="Ministry of Healthcare (Ukraine)">Ministry of Healthcare</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Rada_Reform_341-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Rada_Reform-341">&#91;336&#93;</a></sup> Assisted by deputy Pavlo Kovtoniuk, Suprun first changed the distribution of finances in healthcare.<sup id="cite_ref-Kovtoniuk_342-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Kovtoniuk-342">&#91;337&#93;</a></sup> Funds must follow the patient. General practitioners will provide basic care for patients. The patient will have the right to choose one. Emergency medical service is considered to be fully funded by the state. <a href="/wiki/Emergency_Medicine_Reform_in_Ukraine_since_2016" class="mw-redirect" title="Emergency Medicine Reform in Ukraine since 2016">Emergency Medicine Reform</a> is also an important part of the healthcare reform. In addition, patients who suffer from chronic diseases, which cause a high toll of disability and mortality, are provided with free or low-price medicine.<sup id="cite_ref-Drugs_343-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Drugs-343">&#91;338&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Education">Education</span></h3>

1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/%D0%A0%D0%B5%D0%B7%D0%B8%D0%B4%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%86%D1%96%D1%8F_%D0%BC%D0%B8%D1%82%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%B8%D1%82%D1%96%D0%B2_%D0%91%D1%83%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D0%BD%D0%B8_%D1%96_%D0%94%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%BC%D0%B0%D1%86%D1%96%D1%97_5.jpg/400px-%D0%A0%D0%B5%D0%B7%D0%B8%D0%B4%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%86%D1%96%D1%8F_%D0%BC%D0%B8%D1%82%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%B8%D1%82%D1%96%D0%B2_%D0%91%D1%83%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D0%BD%D0%B8_%D1%96_%D0%94%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%BC%D0%B0%D1%86%D1%96%D1%97_5.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3439" data-file-height="2079" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption">The <a href="/wiki/Residence_of_Bukovinian_and_Dalmatian_Metropolitans" title="Residence of Bukovinian and Dalmatian Metropolitans">Residence of Bukovinian and Dalmatian Metropolitans</a> by <a href="/wiki/Josef_Hl%C3%A1vka" title="Josef Hlávka">Josef Hlávka</a>, 1882, now <a href="/wiki/Chernivtsi_University" title="Chernivtsi University">Chernivtsi University</a></div></div></div></div></div>
<p>According to the <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Ukraine" title="Constitution of Ukraine">Ukrainian constitution</a>, access to free education is granted to all citizens. Complete general secondary education is compulsory in the state schools which constitute the overwhelming majority. Free higher education in state and communal educational establishments is provided on a competitive basis.<sup id="cite_ref-344" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-344">&#91;339&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Because of the Soviet Union's emphasis on total access of education for all citizens, which continues today, the <a href="/wiki/Literacy_rate" class="mw-redirect" title="Literacy rate">literacy rate</a> is an estimated 99.4%.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_52-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-52">&#91;49&#93;</a></sup> Since 2005, an eleven-year school programme has been replaced with a twelve-year one: primary education takes four years to complete (starting at age six), middle education (secondary) takes five years to complete; upper secondary then takes three years.<sup id="cite_ref-345" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-345">&#91;340&#93;</a></sup> Students in the 12th grade take Government tests, which are also referred to as school-leaving exams. These tests are later used for university admissions.
</p><p>Among the oldest is also the <a href="/wiki/Lviv_University" class="mw-redirect" title="Lviv University">Lviv University</a>, founded in 1661. More higher education institutions were set up in the 19th century, beginning with universities in <a href="/wiki/Kharkiv_University" class="mw-redirect" title="Kharkiv University">Kharkiv</a> (1805), <a href="/wiki/Taras_Shevchenko_National_University_of_Kyiv" title="Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv">Kyiv</a> (1834), <a href="/wiki/Odesa_University" title="Odesa University">Odesa</a> (1865) and <a href="/wiki/Chernivtsi_University" title="Chernivtsi University">Chernivtsi</a> (1875) and a number of professional higher education institutions, e.g.: <a href="/wiki/Nizhyn_Pedagogical_University" class="mw-redirect" title="Nizhyn Pedagogical University">Nizhyn Historical and Philological Institute</a> (originally established as the Gymnasium of Higher Sciences in 1805), a Veterinary Institute (1873) and a <a href="/wiki/Kharkiv_Polytechnical_Institute" class="mw-redirect" title="Kharkiv Polytechnical Institute">Technological Institute</a> (1885) in <a href="/wiki/Kharkiv" title="Kharkiv">Kharkiv</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Igor_Sikorsky_Kyiv_Polytechnic_Institute" title="Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute">Polytechnic Institute</a> in Kyiv (1898) and a Higher Mining School (1899) in <a href="/wiki/Dnipro" title="Dnipro">Katerynoslav</a>. Rapid growth followed in the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Soviet_Socialist_Republic" title="Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic">Soviet</a> period. By 1988 the number of higher education institutions increased to 146 with over 850,000 students.<sup id="cite_ref-346" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-346">&#91;341&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The Ukrainian higher education system comprises higher educational establishments, <a href="/wiki/Scientific" class="mw-redirect" title="Scientific">scientific</a> and <a href="/wiki/Methodological" class="mw-redirect" title="Methodological">methodological</a> facilities under national, <a href="/wiki/Municipal_government" class="mw-redirect" title="Municipal government">municipal</a> and self-governing bodies in charge of education.<sup id="cite_ref-347" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-347">&#91;342&#93;</a></sup> The organisation of higher education in Ukraine is built up in accordance with the structure of education of the world's higher <a href="/wiki/Developed_countries" class="mw-redirect" title="Developed countries">developed countries</a>, as is defined by <a href="/wiki/UNESCO" title="UNESCO">UNESCO</a> and the UN.<sup id="cite_ref-348" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-348">&#91;343&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Ukraine produces the fourth largest number of <a href="/wiki/Tertiary_education" title="Tertiary education">post-secondary graduates</a> in Europe, while being ranked seventh in population.<sup id="cite_ref-349" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-349">&#91;344&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Higher_education_in_Ukraine" title="Higher education in Ukraine">Higher education</a> is either state funded or private. Most universities provide subsidised housing for out-of-city students. It is common for libraries to supply required books for all registered students. Ukrainian universities confer two degrees: the bachelor's degree (4&#160;years) and the master's degree (5–6th&#160;year), in accordance with the <a href="/wiki/Bologna_process" class="mw-redirect" title="Bologna process">Bologna process</a>. Historically, <a href="/wiki/Specialist_degree" title="Specialist degree">Specialist degree</a> (usually 5 years) is still also granted; it was the only degree awarded by universities in Soviet times.<sup id="cite_ref-350" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-350">&#91;345&#93;</a></sup> Ukraine was ranked 57th in 2022 in the <a href="/wiki/Global_Innovation_Index" title="Global Innovation Index">Global Innovation Index</a>, down from 49th in 2021<sup id="cite_ref-351" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-351">&#91;346&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-352" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-352">&#91;347&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Regional_differences">Regional differences</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Demographics_of_Ukraine#Regional_differences" title="Demographics of Ukraine">Demographics of Ukraine §&#160;Regional differences</a>, <a href="/wiki/Central_Ukraine" title="Central Ukraine">Central Ukraine</a>, <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Ukraine" title="Eastern Ukraine">Eastern Ukraine</a>, <a href="/wiki/Southern_Ukraine" title="Southern Ukraine">Southern Ukraine</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Western_Ukraine" title="Western Ukraine">Western Ukraine</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ukr_elections_2014_multimandate_okruhs.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Ukr_elections_2014_multimandate_okruhs.png/290px-Ukr_elections_2014_multimandate_okruhs.png" decoding="async" width="290" height="202" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Ukr_elections_2014_multimandate_okruhs.png/435px-Ukr_elections_2014_multimandate_okruhs.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Ukr_elections_2014_multimandate_okruhs.png/580px-Ukr_elections_2014_multimandate_okruhs.png 2x" data-file-width="817" data-file-height="570" /></a><figcaption>The results of the <a href="/wiki/2014_Ukrainian_parliamentary_election" title="2014 Ukrainian parliamentary election">2014 parliamentary election</a> with <a href="/wiki/People%27s_Front_(Ukraine)" title="People&#39;s Front (Ukraine)">People's Front</a> in yellow, <a href="/wiki/Opposition_Bloc" title="Opposition Bloc">Opposition Bloc</a> in blue and <a href="/wiki/Petro_Poroshenko_Bloc" class="mw-redirect" title="Petro Poroshenko Bloc">Petro Poroshenko Bloc</a> in red</figcaption></figure>
<p><a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_language" title="Ukrainian language">Ukrainian</a> is the dominant language in <a href="/wiki/Western_Ukraine" title="Western Ukraine">Western Ukraine</a> and in <a href="/wiki/Central_Ukraine" title="Central Ukraine">Central Ukraine</a>, while <a href="/wiki/Russian_language" title="Russian language">Russian</a> is the dominant language in the cities of <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Ukraine" title="Eastern Ukraine">Eastern Ukraine</a> and <a href="/wiki/Southern_Ukraine" title="Southern Ukraine">Southern Ukraine</a>. In the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_SSR" class="mw-redirect" title="Ukrainian SSR">Ukrainian SSR</a> schools, learning <a href="/wiki/Russian_language" title="Russian language">Russian</a> was mandatory; in modern Ukraine, schools with Ukrainian as the language of instruction offer classes in Russian and in the other minority languages.<sup id="cite_ref-SerhyYUBoaMN_300-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-SerhyYUBoaMN-300">&#91;295&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-353" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-353">&#91;348&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-RatingJuly12_354-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-RatingJuly12-354">&#91;349&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-355" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-355">&#91;350&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On the <a href="/wiki/Russian_language_in_Ukraine" title="Russian language in Ukraine">Russian language</a>, on <a href="/wiki/Soviet_Union" title="Soviet Union">Soviet Union</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_nationalism" title="Ukrainian nationalism">Ukrainian nationalism</a>, opinion in Eastern Ukraine and Southern Ukraine tends to be the exact opposite of those in Western Ukraine; while opinions in Central Ukraine on these topics tend be less extreme.<sup id="cite_ref-RatingJuly12_354-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-RatingJuly12-354">&#91;349&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-356" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-356">&#91;351&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-357" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-357">&#91;352&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-KIISS1313_358-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-KIISS1313-358">&#91;353&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Similar historical cleavages also remain evident at the level of individual social identification. Attitudes toward the most important political issue, relations with Russia, differed strongly between <a href="/wiki/Lviv" title="Lviv">Lviv</a>, identifying more with <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_nationalism" title="Ukrainian nationalism">Ukrainian nationalism</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_Greek_Catholic_Church" title="Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church">Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Donetsk" title="Donetsk">Donetsk</a>, predominantly Russian orientated and favourable to the <a href="/wiki/Soviet_era" class="mw-redirect" title="Soviet era">Soviet era</a>, while in central and southern Ukraine, as well as <a href="/wiki/Kyiv" title="Kyiv">Kyiv</a>, such divisions were less important and there was less antipathy toward people from other regions (a poll by the <a href="/wiki/Research_%26_Branding_Group" title="Research &amp; Branding Group">Research &amp; Branding Group</a> held March 2010 showed that the attitude of the citizens of Donetsk to the citizens of Lviv was 79% positive and that the attitude of the citizens of Lviv to the citizens of Donetsk was 88% positive).<sup id="cite_ref-antipathy_359-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-antipathy-359">&#91;354&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>However, all were united by an overarching Ukrainian identity based on shared economic difficulties, showing that other attitudes are determined more by culture and politics than by demographic differences.<sup id="cite_ref-antipathy_359-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-antipathy-359">&#91;354&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-360" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-360">&#91;355&#93;</a></sup> Surveys of regional identities in Ukraine have shown that the feeling of belonging to a "Soviet identity" is strongest in the <a href="/wiki/Donbas" title="Donbas">Donbas</a> (about 40%) and the Crimea (about 30%).<sup id="cite_ref-361" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-361">&#91;356&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>During <a href="/wiki/Elections_in_Ukraine" title="Elections in Ukraine">elections</a> voters of Western and Central Ukrainian <a href="/wiki/Oblasts_of_Ukraine" title="Oblasts of Ukraine">oblasts</a> (provinces) vote mostly for parties (<a href="/wiki/Our_Ukraine%E2%80%93People%27s_Self-Defense_Bloc" title="Our Ukraine–People&#39;s Self-Defense Bloc">Our Ukraine</a>, <a href="/wiki/All-Ukrainian_Union_%22Fatherland%22" class="mw-redirect" title="All-Ukrainian Union &quot;Fatherland&quot;">Batkivshchyna</a>)<sup id="cite_ref-362" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-362">&#91;357&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-363" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-363">&#91;358&#93;</a></sup> and presidential candidates (<a href="/wiki/Viktor_Yuschenko" class="mw-redirect" title="Viktor Yuschenko">Viktor Yuschenko</a>, <a href="/wiki/Yulia_Tymoshenko" title="Yulia Tymoshenko">Yulia Tymoshenko</a>) with a <a href="/wiki/Pro-Western" class="mw-redirect" title="Pro-Western">pro-Western</a> and state reform <a href="/wiki/Political_platform" class="mw-redirect" title="Political platform">platform</a>, while voters in Southern and Eastern oblasts vote for parties (<a href="/wiki/Communist_Party_of_Ukraine" title="Communist Party of Ukraine">CPU</a>, <a href="/wiki/Party_of_Regions" title="Party of Regions">Party of Regions</a>) and presidential candidates (<a href="/wiki/Viktor_Yanukovych" title="Viktor Yanukovych">Viktor Yanukovych</a>) with a <a href="/wiki/Pro-Russian" class="mw-redirect" title="Pro-Russian">pro-Russian</a> and <a href="/wiki/Status_quo" title="Status quo">status quo</a> platform.<sup id="cite_ref-EWparties_364-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-EWparties-364">&#91;359&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Umland_365-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Umland-365">&#91;360&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-366" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-366">&#91;361&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-367" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-367">&#91;362&#93;</a></sup> However, this geographical division is decreasing.<sup id="cite_ref-368" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-368">&#91;363&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-369" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-369">&#91;364&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-370" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-370">&#91;365&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Culture">Culture</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_culture" class="mw-redirect" title="Ukrainian culture">Ukrainian culture</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Pysanky2011.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Pysanky2011.JPG/220px-Pysanky2011.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="151" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Pysanky2011.JPG/330px-Pysanky2011.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Pysanky2011.JPG/440px-Pysanky2011.JPG 2x" data-file-width="3250" data-file-height="2224" /></a><figcaption>A collection of traditional Ukrainian Easter eggs—<a href="/wiki/Egg_decorating_in_Slavic_culture" title="Egg decorating in Slavic culture">pysanky</a>. The design motifs on pysanky date back to early Slavic cultures.</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Christmas_Vertep_in_Lviv._Photo_256.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/Christmas_Vertep_in_Lviv._Photo_256.jpg/220px-Christmas_Vertep_in_Lviv._Photo_256.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/Christmas_Vertep_in_Lviv._Photo_256.jpg/330px-Christmas_Vertep_in_Lviv._Photo_256.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/Christmas_Vertep_in_Lviv._Photo_256.jpg/440px-Christmas_Vertep_in_Lviv._Photo_256.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4928" data-file-height="3264" /></a><figcaption>Orthodox Christmas celebration in <a href="/wiki/Lviv" title="Lviv">Lviv</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Ukrainian customs are heavily influenced by <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Church" title="Eastern Orthodox Church">Orthodox Christianity</a>, the dominant religion in the country.<sup id="cite_ref-371" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-371">&#91;366&#93;</a></sup> Gender roles also tend to be more traditional, and grandparents play a greater role in bringing up children, than in the West.<sup id="cite_ref-372" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-372">&#91;367&#93;</a></sup> The culture of Ukraine has also been influenced by its eastern and western neighbours, reflected in its <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_architecture" title="Ukrainian architecture">architecture</a>, music and art.<sup id="cite_ref-373" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-373">&#91;368&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The Communist era had quite a strong effect on the art and writing of Ukraine.<sup id="cite_ref-374" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-374">&#91;369&#93;</a></sup> In 1932, Stalin made <a href="/wiki/Socialist_realism" title="Socialist realism">socialist realism</a> state policy in the Soviet Union when he promulgated the decree "On the Reconstruction of Literary and Art Organisations". This greatly stifled creativity. During the 1980s <a href="/wiki/Glasnost" title="Glasnost">glasnost</a> (openness) was introduced and Soviet artists and writers again became free to express themselves as they wanted.<sup id="cite_ref-375" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-375">&#91;370&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>As of 2023<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ukraine&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, UNESCO inscribed 8 properties in Ukraine on the <a href="/wiki/World_Heritage_List" class="mw-redirect" title="World Heritage List">World Heritage List</a>. Ukraine is also known for its decorative and folk traditions such as <a href="/wiki/Petrykivka_painting" title="Petrykivka painting">Petrykivka painting</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kosiv" title="Kosiv">Kosiv</a> ceramics, and <a href="/w/index.php?title=Cossack%27s_songs_of_Dnipropetrovsk_Region&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Cossack&#39;s songs of Dnipropetrovsk Region (page does not exist)">Cossack songs</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-376" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-376">&#91;371&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-377" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-377">&#91;372&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-378" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-378">&#91;373&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-379" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-379">&#91;374&#93;</a></sup> Between February 2022 and March 2023, UNESCO verified the damage to 247 sites, including 107 <a href="/wiki/Religious_site" class="mw-redirect" title="Religious site">religious sites</a>, 89 buildings of artistic or historical interest, 19 monuments and 12 libraries.<sup id="cite_ref-380" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-380">&#91;375&#93;</a></sup> Since January 2023, the historic centre of <a href="/wiki/Odesa" title="Odesa">Odesa</a> has been inscribed on the <a href="/wiki/List_of_World_Heritage_in_Danger" title="List of World Heritage in Danger">List of World Heritage in Danger</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-381" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-381">&#91;376&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The tradition of the <a href="/wiki/Easter_egg" title="Easter egg">Easter egg</a>, known as <a href="/wiki/Pysanky" class="mw-redirect" title="Pysanky">pysanky</a>, has long roots in Ukraine. These eggs were drawn on with wax to create a pattern; then, the dye was applied to give the eggs their pleasant colours, the dye did not affect the previously wax-coated parts of the egg. After the entire egg was dyed, the wax was removed leaving only the colourful pattern. This tradition is thousands of years old, and precedes the arrival of Christianity to Ukraine.<sup id="cite_ref-382" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-382">&#91;377&#93;</a></sup> In the city of <a href="/wiki/Kolomyia" title="Kolomyia">Kolomyia</a> near the foothills of the <a href="/wiki/Carpathian_Mountains" title="Carpathian Mountains">Carpathian Mountains</a>, the museum of Pysanka was built in 2000 and won a nomination as the monument of modern Ukraine in 2007, part of the <a href="/wiki/Seven_Wonders_of_Ukraine" title="Seven Wonders of Ukraine">Seven Wonders of Ukraine</a> action.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Libraries">Libraries</span></h3>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Vernadsky_National_Library_of_Ukraine" title="Vernadsky National Library of Ukraine">Vernadsky National Library of Ukraine</a>, is the main academic library and main scientific information centre in Ukraine.
</p><p>During the <a href="/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" class="mw-redirect" title="2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine">2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine</a> the Russians bombed the Maksymovych Scientific Library of the Taras Shevchenko Kyiv National University, Vernadsky National Library of Ukraine, the National Scientific Medical Library of Ukraine and the Kyiv city youth library.<sup id="cite_ref-383" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-383">&#91;378&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Literature">Literature</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_literature" title="Ukrainian literature">Ukrainian literature</a></div>
<p>Ukrainian literature has origins in <a href="/wiki/Old_Church_Slavonic" title="Old Church Slavonic">Old Church Slavonic</a> writings, which was used as a <a href="/wiki/Liturgy" title="Liturgy">liturgical</a> and <a href="/wiki/Literary_language" title="Literary language">literary language</a> following <a href="/wiki/Christianization_of_Kievan_Rus%27" title="Christianization of Kievan Rus&#39;">Christianization</a> in the 10th and 11th centuries.<sup id="cite_ref-ualit_384-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ualit-384">&#91;379&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-ualitmsn_385-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ualitmsn-385">&#91;380&#93;</a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template noprint noexcerpt Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:NOTRS" class="mw-redirect" title="Wikipedia:NOTRS"><span title="This claim needs references to better sources. (December 2022)">better&#160;source&#160;needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup><sup id="cite_ref-386" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-386">&#91;f&#93;</a></sup> Other writings from the time include <a href="/wiki/Chronicle" title="Chronicle">chronicles</a>, the most significant of which was the <i><a href="/wiki/Primary_Chronicle" title="Primary Chronicle">Primary Chronicle</a></i>.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (December 2022)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> Literary activity faced a sudden decline after the <a href="/wiki/Mongol_invasion_of_Kievan_Rus%27" title="Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus&#39;">Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus'</a>, before seeing a revival beginning in the 14th&#160;century, and was advanced in the 16th&#160;century with the invention of the <a href="/wiki/Printing_press" title="Printing press">printing press</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-ualit_384-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ualit-384">&#91;379&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/%D0%A2._%D0%93._%D0%A8%D0%B5%D0%B2%D1%87%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%BA%D0%BE._%D0%9A%D0%B2%D1%96%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%8C_1859.jpg/294px-%D0%A2._%D0%93._%D0%A8%D0%B5%D0%B2%D1%87%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%BA%D0%BE._%D0%9A%D0%B2%D1%96%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%8C_1859.jpg
